title: Cerebrospinal fluid amyloid and neurodegeneration biomarkers in the diagnosis and prognosis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: a multicohort observational study.
abstract: Neurofilament light chain (NfL) is an established biomarker for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). However, it remains unclear whether biomarkers reflecting amyloid-β metabolism (Aβ), tau (phosphorylated tau, pTau), and astrogliosis (glial fibrillary acidic protein, GFAP) can complement NfL in clinical applications. It is also unclear how Alzheimer's disease (AD) co-pathology affects disease progression in ALS. We studied 264 patients with ALS and 164 disease-control participants, analysing baseline cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) NfL, Aβ peptides, pTau181, pTau217, and GFAP. A two-step diagnostic strategy was examined in individuals with intermediate NfL values, using machine-learning models. Prognostic associations were evaluated using linear mixed-effects and Cox models adjusted for established predictors; survival was additionally examined in pooled analyses including an external ALS cohort (n = 153). Patients with ALS exhibited higher CSF NfL, Aβ38, Aβ40, Aβ42, pTau181, and pTau217 than controls, even within Aβ-negative subgroups. NfL discriminated ALS from controls with an AUC of 0.85 (0.82-0.88), which increased to 0.90 (0.88-0.92) in machine-learning models incorporating additional biomarkers. The machine-learning models maintained a high positive predictive value (0.90) for classifying cases with intermediate NfL values. Significant Aβ × NfL interactions were observed for longitudinal functional decline, and pooled survival analyses showed stronger associations between NfL and survival in the Aβ-positive ALS subgroup (14%) than in the Aβ-negative ALS subgroup (HR 4.02 [2.17-7.45] vs 1.62 [1.36-1.92]). Multiple biomarker assessments can reduce misclassification of individuals with intermediate NfL values. CSF Aβ positivity modified the association between baseline NfL and disease progression. Personalised diagnosis and prognosis based on fine-grained co-pathology evaluation may enhance clinical management of ALS. This study was primarily supported by JST SPRING (JPMJSP2125). A complete list of funding organisations is provided in Acknowledgements.

title: Tumor innervation in non-central nervous system tumors: origins, mechanisms, and phenotypic plasticity.
abstract: The peripheral nervous system has emerged as an important regulator of solid tumor biology. We synthesize recent advances in cancer neuroscience, focusing on three interconnected themes: the cellular origins of tumor-associated nerves, the molecular mechanisms that govern neural recruitment and remodeling, and the resulting phenotypic plasticity within the tumor microenvironment. Tumor innervation arises through axon extension from pre-existing nerves, recruitment of neural precursors, and neuron-like transdifferentiation of non-neuronal cells. These processes are driven by neurotrophic factors, axon guidance cues, extracellular vesicles, and stress-associated pathways. The functional consequences of innervation are context-dependent, with sympathetic, parasympathetic, and sensory inputs exerting distinct effects across tumor types and stages. We conclude by outlining key challenges and future directions for therapeutic translation.

title: SIRT5 Attenuates Traumatic Brain Injury by Preserving OPA1-Mediated Mitochondrial Fusion and Limiting Oxidative Stress.
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress are central pathological drivers of disease progression following traumatic brain injury (TBI). Sirtuin 5 (SIRT5), a predominantly mitochondrial NAD+-dependent deacylase, plays critical roles in mitochondrial quality control, redox homeostasis, and metabolic regulation. This study aims to define the upstream regulatory machinery controlling SIRT5 stability and to identify the downstream pathway linking SIRT5 to mitochondrial remodeling after TBI. In this study, we demonstrated that TBI promotes neuronal SIRT5 protein degradation via a synergistic regulatory mechanism involving USP7 and TRIM21. Using neuron-specific Sirt5 conditional knockout mice, we found that SIRT5 deficiency exacerbates TBI-induced mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative damage, cerebral edema, and neurological deficits. SIRT5 regulates OPA1 expression through a MEF2A-dependent mechanism, thereby preserving mitochondrial structure and function and alleviating oxidative injury. The protective effects of neuronal SIRT5 overexpression were abolished in mice lacking Opa1 specifically in neurons, confirming that OPA1 is a critical downstream effector of SIRT5-mediated neuroprotection. Finally, rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG)-conjugated extracellular vesicles loaded with SIRT5 mRNA demonstrated both efficacy and safety in preclinical TBI models. This study identifies the USP7/TRIM21-SIRT5-MEF2A-OPA1 axis as a novel regulatory cascade that governs the transition between adaptive and maladaptive mitochondrial remodeling after TBI, a concept with broad implications for acute brain injury and neurodegeneration. This study defines the USP7/TRIM21-SIRT5-MEF2A-OPA1 axis as a novel regulatory cascade that controls mitochondrial remodeling after TBI. SIRT5 acts through a MEF2A-dependent mechanism to maintain OPA1 expression and mitochondrial fusion, and its transient restoration via RVG-EV delivery of SIRT5 mRNA is a promising therapeutic strategy. Antioxid. Redox Signal. 00, 000-000.

title: The Lysosomal Clock: Are We Only as Old as Our Lysosomes?
abstract: Lysosomes are a major organelle involved in intracellular degradation, membrane traffic and metabolic signaling, but how their biochemical composition changes during normal aging remains poorly defined. Puszynska and colleagues now combine lysosome purification with metabolomics and lipidomics across tissues, species and ages to reveal a conserved signature of lysosomal aging characterized by accumulation of glycerophosphodiesters (GPDs) and cystine and remodeling of bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP). Strikingly, these changes are largely obscured in whole-tissue analyses and resemble metabolic abnormalities associated with lysosomal storage disorders, including CLN3 disease and cystinosis. The signature develops progressively with age, can predict chronological age, and is attenuated by caloric restriction in peripheral tissues but not in the brain. Within the brain, age-dependent metabolite accumulation is particularly prominent in microglia and is also detected in neurons, linking lysosomal aging to cell populations central to neurodegenerative disease. These findings define an organelle-level metabolic clock, suggesting that one might be only as young as one's lysosomes. Establishing whether GPDs, cystine and BMP remodeling merely mark lysosomal age or actively contribute to declining lysosomal degradation and membrane traffic may uncover a metabolic connection between physiological aging, lysosomal storage disorders and vulnerability to late-onset neurodegeneration.

title: Old woman with left lower extremity pain.
ASFNR Clinical State of Practice Statement on Imaging of Chronic Subdural Hematoma.
abstract: The efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) has heightened interest in imaging biomarkers that may reflect neomembrane activity, predict recurrence, and identify patients most likely to benefit from treatment. Characterization of hematoma internal architecture, referred to as the imaging phenotype, may provide indirect information regarding the biological activity and maturation of the neomembrane. However, imaging phenotype has not been incorporated into randomized trials or validated treatment-selection algorithms, and standardized definitions and reporting remain lacking. The American Society of Functional Neuroradiology Clinical Practice Committee developed this State of Practice statement through expert consensus and review of the available literature. Noncontrast CT (NCCT) remains the primary imaging modality for cSDH assessment. Hematoma burden should be characterized by maximum thickness measured perpendicular to the inner table, midline shift, and, when appropriate, volume. Volume may be estimated using the ABC/2 formula, whereas segmentation is more accurate for irregular, crescentic, or multiloculated collections when available. Internal architecture should be described using the Nakaguchi framework of homogeneous, laminar, separated, and trabecular phenotypes, with mixed or transitional features explicitly reported. Advanced techniques, including dual-energy CT, photon-counting CT, MRI, and arterial spin labeling, may provide information regarding membrane activity but are supported by limited, largely single-center evidence and currently have a problem-solving rather than routine role. Standardized reporting and prospective validation are needed before imaging phenotype or advanced-imaging biomarkers can guide treatment selection.

title: Tea polyphenols amplify oxidative stress-induced eradication of Staphylococcus aureus by disrupting the hydrogen sulfide (H2S) signaling pathway.
abstract: Endogenous hydrogen sulfide (H2S) acts as a pivotal shield for Staphylococcus aureus against oxidative stress. Although tea polyphenols (TPs) are established antibacterial agents, their precise mechanistic impact on H2S-linked redox regulation has yet to be fully elucidated. Here, we test the hypothesis that TPs exert their bactericidal effect on S. aureus by compromising its intrinsic H2S-mediated antioxidant defense system. DL-Propargylglycine (PAG) was used to construct an H2S synthesis-inhibited model (designated WT + inh). The response of this model to TPs was evaluated against that of the wild-type (WT) strain by growth curve analysis, flow cytometry analysis, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). In addition, reactive oxygen species (ROS), antioxidant enzyme activities, including superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT), the oxidative damage marker malondialdehyde (MDA), and the expression of oxidative stress- and sulfur metabolism-related genes were determined. Finally, exogenous H2S supplementation was used to examine whether sulfide could modify the response to TPs. PAG treatment significantly enhanced bacterial susceptibility to TPs, concomitant with increased cell death and exacerbated morphological damage. Intracellular activities of SOD and CAT were reduced, whereas ROS and MDA levels were significantly elevated. Exogenous H2S modulated the growth inhibitory effects of TPs. The TP-associated oxidative damage coincided with changes in H2S-related sulfur metabolism and antioxidant gene expression. These findings support an association between H2S-related antioxidant defense and the susceptibility of S. aureus to TPs, providing a basis for further investigation of H2S metabolism in tea polyphenol-based antibacterial strategies.

title: Interpreting metabolite associations and proposed biosynthetic routes in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum-fermented Porphyra haitanensis.
abstract: The recent study by Li et al. links Lactiplantibacillus plantarum fermentation of Porphyra haitanensis with enhanced in vitro lipid-lowering-related activities, metabolomic remodeling, and beverage development. We welcome this integrative approach but suggest that the mechanistic interpretation of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and p-coumaric acid (pCA) should be calibrated to the evidence. Untargeted LC-MS supports fermentation-associated changes in relative abundance, yet metabolite identity and concentration require orthogonal confirmation and targeted quantification. Likewise, accumulation of pCA cannot distinguish de novo synthesis from release of pre-existing phenolics or altered turnover, and neither GABA nor pCA was directly shown to mediate the observed enzyme- or micelle-related effects. The marked rise in pancreatic lipase inhibition after formulation and pasteurization further warrants vehicle and pH-matched controls to exclude matrix effects. We propose targeted validation of metabolite identity, flux, enzyme activity, and compound-specific function to strengthen the proposed biosynthetic and functional links.

title: Interpreting glycine-associated phenotypes in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum: the need for strain-specific and medium-controlled evidence.
abstract: Han et al. report that glycine supplementation alters growth-associated readouts and improves bile and osmotic stress tolerance in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum KCCM 11322. We agree that these phenotypes may be relevant to starter-culture optimization, but the mechanistic attribution to metabolic remodeling remains incomplete. Pathway inference was based on a reference L. plantarum annotation rather than the KCCM 11322 genome; experiments used chemically undefined MRS, so 0 mM denotes no added glycine rather than a glycine-free baseline; and pH was not systematically controlled. The divergence between visible biomass, OD600, and CFU at high glycine concentrations further emphasizes the need to separate biomass accumulation from viable growth. Strain-specific genomics, defined-medium experiments, pH-matched controls, and targeted metabolic measurements would clarify whether glycine acts as a nutrient, physicochemical modifier, or regulator of metabolic flux.

title: Biosynthetic mechanisms and application of bioactive compounds associated with in vitro lipid-lowering-related activities produced by Lactiplantibacillus plantarum fermentation of Porphyra haitanensis.
abstract: Fourth-harvest Porphyra haitanensis (FPH) is abundant but underutilized because of undesirable flavor and poor palatability. Microbial fermentation is an effective strategy for the high-value utilization of FPH. The metabolic basis and application potential of bioactive compounds accumulated during FPH fermentation by Lactiplantibacillus plantarum and associated with in vitro lipid digestion and absorption inhibitory activities were investigated. The results demonstrated that fermentation increased the maximal inhibition rates of pancreatic lipase, cholesterol esterase, and cholesterol micellar solubility to 68.27 ± 0.81%, 68.97 ± 0.61%, and 72.72 ± 0.52%, respectively, and increased glycocholate and taurocholate binding to 53.79 ± 0.74% and 55.91 ± 1.45%, respectively. Metabolomics showed extensive metabolic remodeling and suggested γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and p-coumaric acid (pCA) as putative candidate metabolites associated with the enhanced in vitro lipid-lowering-related activities and flavor quality. KEGG analysis indicated that the accumulation of GABA and pCA may be related to glutamate metabolism, substrate degradation, and associated enzyme-catalyzed pathways, providing a potential metabolic explanation rather than direct evidence of biosynthetic mechanisms. A fermented FPH beverage was subsequently formulated, and the optimal formulation consisted of 70% fermented liquor, 10 g/100 mL erythritol, and 0.5 g/100 mL sodium citrate. The formulated beverage was further subjected to pasteurization, and 90 °C for 10 min was selected as the final processing condition for the subsequent storage evaluation. This treatment maintained a high level of in vitro lipid-lowering-related activity, with a pancreatic lipase inhibition rate of 93.02 ± 1.75%, while providing better physical stability. The shelf life was predicted to be 46 days at 20 °C and 308 days at 4 °C based on the storage stability model. This study provides a theoretical basis and technical support for the high-value utilization of low-quality seaweed.

title: Glycine supplementation reshapes metabolism and enhances growth and stress tolerance in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum.
abstract: Glycine plays a pivotal role in microbial metabolism, yet its function in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum remains incompletely understood. This study investigates the metabolic and physiological impact of glycine supplementation using an integrated computational and experimental approach. In silico KEGG pathway mapping based on the L. plantarum reference genome annotation (lpl, T00115) indicated incomplete representation of the glycine cleavage system (M00621) and betaine degradation pathway (M00975), suggesting possible pathway-level limitations in glycine catabolism and C1-unit generation. Molecular docking indicated that glycine could be accommodated within the binding pockets of selected enzymes associated with glycine-related and folate-dependent pathways. STRING network analysis further suggested possible connections between these proteins and threonine, methionine, and lysine biosynthetic networks. In vitro assays showed that 10 mM glycine produced the highest visible biomass accumulation, with higher glycine concentrations increased biomass accumulation based on OD600 values. Interestingly, glycine exposure also modified colony morphology and shifted antibiotic susceptibility profiles, particularly to β-lactams. Moreover, glycine supplementation improved bacterial survival under bile salt and osmotic stress conditions. These findings suggest that exogenous glycine may contribute to biomass-associated responses and stress-related phenotypes in L. plantarum under the tested conditions. Furthermore, phenotypic and reference genome-informed evidence shows that glycine availability is associated with growth- and stress-related responses in L. plantarum KCCM 11322, providing a basis for further mechanistic validation of amino acid supplementation in food microbiology-related applications.

Cuttlefish use the negation of dead prey to judge food value in foraging decision.
abstract: Understanding how targeted prey conditions influence foraging decisions is a fundamental issue in animal behaviour. The present study investigated whether cuttlefish use prey liveness to assess overall food quality. Cuttlefish were allowed to choose between different levels of prey freshness and quantity. Experiments 1 and 2 examined cuttlefish choices between one live shrimp alone and one live shrimp paired with either one or four freshly dead shrimps. Experiment 3 evaluated their preferences of one live shrimp paired with either one freshly dead shrimp or one hourly dead shrimp. Experiment 4 assessed their choices between these two types of dead shrimp alone. Results showed that cuttlefish significantly avoided the side containing one live shrimp paired with one freshly dead shrimp, and this avoidance increased proportionally with the quantity of dead shrimp. However, cuttlefish choice did not differ significantly between freshly and hourly dead shrimps. These findings suggest that the presence of dead shrimp decreases a cuttlefish's perceived food value, and that motionless prey, regardless of their condition, serve as a negative indicator of overall food quality. This study demonstrates that cuttlefish assess total prey value based on the negation of dead prey, a mental process of intentionally removing hindrances during evaluation.

title: Dynamic facial movements shape how confident speakers appear.
abstract: Human communication is inherently multimodal, relying on signals conveyed through speech, vocal tone and facial movements. While gestures and vocal cues are known to influence how speech is understood, the role of facial movements remains poorly specified. Here, we test whether dynamic facial movements shape how spoken responses are interpreted by systematically modulating listener inferences of speaker confidence and doubt. Using a data-driven reverse-correlation approach and a generative model of facial behaviour, we manipulated speakers' upper-face movements while holding verbal content constant. On each trial, participants (n = 44; UK English and Mandarin Chinese speakers) rated the confidence of speakers responding to questions (e.g. 'Would they make a good leader?') on a five-point scale across 1800 trials. We find that opposing facial movements bias these inferences: eye closure and brow raising are associated with confidence, whereas brow lowering and eye tightening are associated with doubt. Signal amplitude further shapes these inferences, primarily by intensifying perceived doubt for doubt-associated movements. These mappings are largely shared between the two cultural groups, indicating common signal-inference relationships alongside differences in the weighting of specific cues. Together, these findings show that facial movements provide graded social signals that systematically shape how spoken responses are interpreted.

title: Proteomic analysis identifies proteins involved in increased vascular permeability in vestibular schwannoma patients.
abstract: Vestibular schwannomas (VS) are benign neoplasms of the VIII cranial nerve; they account for 6-8% of all intracranial tumors and about 80% of tumors of the cerebellopontine angle. Cystic forms of VS may be particularly dangerous, as they demonstrate faster growth and worse postoperative outcomes. In this study, we performed proteomic analysis of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples obtained from patients with solid and cystic forms of VS, as well as cyst fluid from patients with cystic VS. CSF samples from patients with hemifacial spasm were used as controls. Mass spectrometric (MS) analysis resulted in identification of 816 proteins in all samples and 111 proteins were upregulated in samples obtained from VS patients compared to the control group. The upregulated proteins belonged to the groups of components and regulators of the complement system, proteins associated with glucose and lipid metabolism. MS analysis of CSF obtained from patients with cystic and solid forms of VS resulted in identification of two proteomic clusters enriched in proteins associated with the development of the nervous system, cell adhesion, and myelination processes. The data obtained suggest the involvement of these biological processes in the pathogenesis of cystic VS. SIGNIFICANCE: This study provides a comprehensive proteomic characterization of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and cyst fluid from patients with solid and cystic vestibular schwannomas (VS), offering valuable insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying these tumors. Our discovery that complement system components and regulators are consistently upregulated in CSF and cyst fluid from VS patients, along with proteins involved in lipid metabolism, points to a potential mechanism of blood-brain barrier disruption and cyst formation, which is particularly relevant given the more aggressive clinical course of cystic VS. These findings not only contribute to understanding of VS pathogenesis but also suggest candidate protein targets for future diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic strategies, particularly for the more challenging cystic form of the disease.

title: Obesity-induced oxidative stress and cGMP depletion suppress cerebellar α2,3-Na+,K+-ATPase activity in female mice.
authors: Lopes de Morais Toledo Marina Marques
abstract: Obesity is a major metabolic disorder linked to neuroinflammation and cognitive decline. Beyond hypothalamic alterations, emerging evidence indicates that extra-hypothalamic regions, including the cerebellum, are vulnerable to obesity-induced neurotoxicity. This study investigated whether high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity causes cerebellar oxidative stress, impairs Na+,K+-ATPase (NKA) activity, and triggers molecular features resembling brain aging in female Balb/C mice. Chronic 10-week HFD intake established a marked obese phenotype, characterized by increased adiposity, fasting hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, and elevated serum TNF-α. In the cerebellum, obesity induced a selective, expression-independent reduction in α2,3-NKA isoform activity, accompanied by a marked depletion of tissue cGMP levels. This functional impairment was driven by an oxidative microenvironment, evidenced by elevated H2O2 and TBARS levels and increased 4-HNE accumulation. Concomitantly, obese animals mounted an adaptive antioxidant response characterized by increased GST, GR, and GPx activities, reduced glutathione (GSH) consumption, and ERK1/2-mediated nuclear translocation of Nrf2, alongside structural membrane lipid remodeling (elevated cholesterol and reduced phospholipids). In summary, chronic obesity induces robust lipoxidative stress and suppresses cerebellar cGMP signaling and α2,3-NKA activity in female mice, recapitulating key molecular hallmarks of natural brain aging.

title: Machine learning of connectome-wide functional connectivity in spinal muscular atrophy.
abstract: While traditional view posed SMA as a pure motor neuron disorder, accumulating evidence pointed to the broader involvement of central nervous system. This study aimed to combined connectome-wide resting-state functional connectivity with machine learning algorithms to investigate the underlying brain mechanisms in SMA and capture the potential neuroimaging biomarker. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging were acquired from 43 SMA (26 SMA type 2 and 17 type 3) and 45 healthy controls (HCs). Connectome-wide functional connectivity, defined based on the Automated Anatomical Labeling 116 atlas (AAL116), combined with machine learning algorithms including logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF) were conducted for SMA vs HCs and SMA type 2 vs 3 classification. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithm was used to quantify the contribution of individual connections. Connectome-wide functional connectivity allowed individual classification of SMA and HCs with stable performance across machine learning models. The majority of the most discriminative functional connectivity involved the high-level associative regions and cerebellum, subserving sensory and motor processing. Furthermore, the functional connectivity between right superior parietal gyrus and right inferior temporal gyrus was positively correlated with motor function. In conclusion, our study provided connectome-wide evidence that functional connectivity patterns involving high-level associative cortices and the cerebellum could distinguish SMA from HCs using machine learning. The identified connectivity features offer new insight into the distributed brain pathology of SMA beyond the traditional classical motor neuron view, and may serve as promising neuroimaging marker for this disease.

title: AMPK signaling in cancer: Molecular insights and therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) is a highly conserved serine/threonine kinase regarded as an indispensable energy sensor during metabolic stress, coordinating diverse biological processes, including glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, mitochondrial dynamics, and multiple stress-responsive signaling pathways. Growing evidence shows that dysregulated AMPK signaling plays closely linked roles in tumorigenesis. Depending on the context, AMPK signaling can suppress or promote tumor growth. Mechanistically, dysregulated AMPK kinase activity contributes to metabolic reprogramming, mitochondrial dysfunction, and epigenetic alterations, all recognized hallmarks of cancer. Consequently, targeting AMPK signaling has emerged as a promising strategy for cancer therapy. In this review, we summarize the molecular mechanisms regulating AMPK signaling, discuss its dual functions in tumor biology, highlight recent advances in AMPK-targeted therapeutic strategies, and address current challenges and future perspectives for the clinical translation of AMPK-targeted cancer therapy.

title: UBL3 Modification Reduces Nuclear POLE Levels to Potentiate Antitumor Immunity in Aero-upper Digestive Squamous Cell Carcinomas.
abstract: While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized treatment of the patients with aero-upper digestive squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs), including esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), only a subset of patients benefit from ICIs, therefore entailing exploration of the mechanisms to regulate treatment responsiveness. POLE, as a subunit of DNA polymerase ε, possesses 3'-5' proofreading activity, and its mutations have been associated with favourable response to ICIs in several solid tumors. However, post-translational modification (PTM) of POLE and its impact on the therapeutic efficacy of ICIs are unknown. Here, this study demonstrates that ubiquitin-like protein 3 (Ubl3), whose expression is markedly downregulated in SCCs, covalently binds to Pole, reduces nuclear Pole levels, triggers DNA damage, and activates cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Notably, Ubl3 modification of Pole significantly primes the local immune microenvironment to mitigate the growth of murine aero-upper digestive SCC cells and boost the efficacy of αPD-1 treatment in vivo. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis further revealed that UBL3 expression is positively correlated with better clinical outcomes in a cohort of ESCC patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy combined with αPD-1. Together, our findings unravel UBL3 modification as a novel PTM mechanism governing subcellular location of POLE and its influence on immunotherapy responsiveness, thus making UBL3 modification as a promising immunomodulatory approach to enhance immunotherapy efficacy in patients with aero-upper digestive SCCs.

title: Right putaminal gray matter change tracks psychomotor recovery after accelerated iTBS in melancholic treatment-resistant depression.
abstract: Psychomotor retardation is a prominent and disabling feature of melancholic depression. Accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (aiTBS) may hasten antidepressant effects, but neural substrates of early symptom improvement remain unclear. Given the central role of frontostriatal circuitry in motivation and behavioral activation, structural alterations in the striatum may represent a possible neural substrate of early therapeutic change. Structural MRI was acquired from 61 patients with melancholic TRD and 77 healthy controls, and voxel-based morphometry was used to assess baseline striatal gray matter volume differences. Patients then underwent a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial of left dorsolateral prefrontal aiTBS, comprising 20 sessions over four days. In 50 patients with complete pre- and post-treatment data, we tested whether GMV change in the baseline-identified striatal region was associated with clinical change in the active and sham groups (n = 25 each). Patients showed greater right putamen GMV than controls at baseline. After active aiTBS, greater right putamen GMV increase was associated with greater psychomotor retardation improvement. This association was absent after sham stimulation and was not observed for overall depression severity. The right putamen appears structurally altered in melancholic TRD. After active aiTBS, short-term putamen GMV increase was associated with psychomotor rather than broader depressive improvement. This pattern should not be interpreted as structural normalization but may reflect a relationship between putaminal change and early psychomotor recovery.

title: Resting-state fMRI biomarkers of surgical outcome in temporal lobe epilepsy: Network reorganization, rsfMRI-based prediction models, and cognition - A systematic review.
abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a network disorder extending beyond the structurally defined epileptogenic zone. Resting-state functional MRI (rsfMRI) may provide information on brain network alterations relevant to seizure outcome and cognitive risk after epilepsy surgery. We reviewed rsfMRI studies in TLE surgical cohorts to evaluate postoperative network changes, preoperative predictors of seizure outcome, and associations between functional connectivity and cognition. This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. Fifteen studies were included, comprising 474 TLE patients who underwent resective epilepsy surgery and had at least 1 year of follow-up. Studies were reviewed for patient population, surgery, rsfMRI methodology, networks or regions, outcome definition, postoperative network changes, and cognitive assessments. Despite heterogeneity in patient selection, surgery, rsfMRI analysis, and outcome definition, studies consistently reported reduced DMN-related connectivity in TLE compared with healthy controls. Postoperative functional connectivity in seizure-free patients shifted toward healthy controls patterns in few studies. Preoperative rsfMRI-based prediction models showed promising accuracy for predicting seizure outcome but were generally developed in small cohorts and lacked external validation. Evidence relating rsfMRI to cognition was limited, but implicated thalamic, ascending reticular activating system, and thalamo-occipital connectivity in attention, language, and executive functions. RsfMRI is a promising research biomarker for network-level risk stratification in TLE surgery, particularly for seizure outcome prediction and postoperative network reorganization. Current evidence remains insufficient for clinical implementation. Future studies require larger homogeneous multicenter cohorts, standardized acquisition and preprocessing, consistent outcome definitions, systematic postoperative rsfMRI, neuropsychological assessment, and external validation of prediction models.

title: Interpersonal neural synchrony and parent-child behaviors during naturalistic interactions: A systematic review.
abstract: Interpersonal neural synchrony (INS), defined as the temporal alignment of neural activity between socially interacting individuals, has been proposed as an index of parent-child interaction quality. However, its relationship with moment-to-moment adjustment of parent-child behavior remains insufficiently understood. This systematic review examined associations between INS and observable behavior during naturalistic parent-child interactions, the factors influencing these associations, and the methods used to investigate them. Following PRISMA guidelines, systematic searches of Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect identified 15 peer-reviewed empirical studies involving children from preschool age to early adolescence. INS-behavior associations were heterogeneous across studies. Higher INS was most consistently associated with mutual engagement, shared positive affect, and supportive parenting, whereas findings concerning reciprocity, responsiveness, and child agency were more context-dependent. Time-resolved analyses further indicated that INS fluctuated in relation to specific behavioral events and revealed temporally asymmetric patterns in which parent or child neural activity preceded that of the interaction partner. However, these patterns do not establish causal directionality and may partly reflect shared exposure to task-related or interactional inputs. Task structure and the availability of direct social cues appeared to shape INS-behavior associations, while parental stress and child social functioning emerged as potential sources of variability in INS. Methodologically, the findings highlight the value of combining micro- and macro-level behavioral coding with time-resolved and directionality-sensitive analyses, alongside stronger controls for spurious synchrony and common inputs. Given the limited number and methodological heterogeneity of available studies, the findings should be regarded as preliminary and primarily hypothesis-generating.

title: Pharmacological TRPM8 blockade reprograms patient-derived intestinal fibroblasts and mitigates experimental fibrosis through modulation of myofibroblast activation.
abstract: Intestinal fibrosis is a major long-term complication mostly prevalent in Crohn's disease (CD) and remains without approved antifibrotic therapies. Transient receptor potential melastatin 8 (TRPM8) is a pharmacologically targetable ion channel involved in inflammatory regulation, but its contribution to intestinal fibrotic remodeling is unknown. This study investigated TRPM8 association with human stenotic CD and whether pharmacological TRPM8 modulation limits fibroblast activation and experimental intestinal fibrosis. TRPM8 expression was increased in stenotic ileocolonic tissues from CD patients and in primary patient-derived intestinal fibroblasts. In these cells, the TRPM8 antagonist AMTB reduced proliferation and migration at non-cytotoxic concentration and attenuated the expression of fibroblast activation, matrix and myofibroblast-associated markers. In mice with chronic 2,4,6-trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid (TNBS)-induced intestinal fibrosis, AMTB reduced disease activity and endoscopic severity and attenuated stromal remodeling-associated gene expression. Histological analyses further showed reduced tissue injury and collagen remodeling, supported by Masson's Trichrome staining and quantitative analysis of Picrosirius Red. In contrast, pharmacological TRPM8 activation with WS12 did not significantly modify fibroblast proliferation in vitro or the evaluated clinical, endoscopic and molecular readouts in vivo. AMTB also reduced the TNBS-induced T helper 17 response without reducing interleukin-23 production by colonic mononuclear phagocytes. Finally, fibroblasts isolated from AMTB-treated fibrotic mice displayed reduced expansion, lower collagenogenic gene expression, reduced contractile/activated fibroblast markers and decreased actin cytoskeletal remodeling ex vivo. Overall, these findings identify TRPM8 as a druggable regulator of fibroblast-driven intestinal remodeling and support TRPM8 antagonism as a candidate antifibrotic strategy for stricturing CD.

title: From Blue Dye to Multimodal-Guided Surgery: The Evolution of Sentinel Lymph Node Mapping in Vulvar Cancer - A Narrative Review.
abstract: The surgical management of inguinofemoral lymph nodes in early-stage vulvar cancer has progressively shifted from complete lymphadenectomy toward selective sentinel lymph node (SLN) biopsy, reducing treatment-related morbidity while preserving oncologic safety. This narrative review summarizes the historical, technical, and clinical evolution of SLN mapping, from vital blue dyes to radiotracer-based validation and contemporary multimodal image-guided approaches. A literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus was performed through May 2026, including landmark prospective studies, multicenter validation trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines, and studies evaluating indocyanine green (ICG) and hybrid radioactive-fluorescent tracers. Early blue dye studies established the feasibility of lymphatic mapping, whereas technetium-99m, lymphoscintigraphy, and gamma-probe guidance provided the reproducibility required for prospective validation. GROINSS-V I supported safe omission of complete inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy in carefully selected SLN-negative patients, complemented by diagnostic validation in GOG-173; subsequent evidence linked SLN tumor burden to prognosis and enabled risk-adapted management of positive nodes. ICG-based near-infrared fluorescence has emerged as a valuable tool for real-time visualization and may improve intraoperative guidance. However, most comparative studies have evaluated fluorescence after radiotracer-based localization or defined the SLN according to technetium uptake, limiting conclusions regarding stand-alone interchangeability. Current evidence therefore supports ICG primarily as an adjunct within multimodal mapping rather than as a validated replacement for technetium-99m. Future progress should focus on standardized fluorescence protocols, rigorously sequenced ICG-first validation, hybrid radioactive-fluorescent strategies, and integration of imaging-derived and artificial intelligence-based tools into individualized groin management.

title: Tele-Based Ischemic Conditioning for Chronic Stroke: Safety, Feasibility, and Preliminary Neurophysiological and Motor Effects.
journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
abstract: To examine the safety and feasibility of a two-week (seven-session) tele-based ischemic conditioning (tele-IC) intervention in individuals with chronic stroke and to explore secondary neurophysiological and motor outcomes. Ten individuals with chronic stroke (8 males; age 61.7 ± 7.3 years; time since stroke 11.5 ± 7.5 years; Fugl-Meyer Lower Extremity score 20.5 ± 6.6) completed tele-IC. The primary outcomes were safety and feasibility. Safety was assessed through monitoring of IC-related adverse events and side effects across sessions; feasibility was evaluated through screening-to-enrollment, retention, intervention adherence, tolerability, and acceptability. Secondary exploratory outcomes included corticomotor excitability, transcallosal inhibition, lower-limb strength, paretic ankle motor control, and gait speed. Outcomes were assessed before and 24 hours after the intervention. Across 70 tele-IC sessions, no serious adverse events occurred, and all 10 participants completed all seven sessions. Acceptability was high, including ratings for safety (4.9/5), remote assistance (4.8/5), and overall satisfaction (4.8/5). Exploratory analyses showed increased transcallosal inhibition (d_z = 0.929, p = 0.017), changes in bilateral lower-limb strength (d_z = 0.873-1.756), and shorter paretic ankle reaction time (d_z = 0.844, p = 0.049). Corticomotor excitability and gait speed did not significantly change. In this small, uncontrolled pilot study, synchronously supervised tele-IC was delivered with complete intervention adherence, no serious adverse events, and high participant acceptability. Exploratory secondary neurophysiological and motor findings require confirmation in larger controlled trials.

title: White Matter Hyperintensities of Presumed Vascular Origin: Current Understanding of Development and Progression.
journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
abstract: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) of presumed vascular origin are among the most common MRI manifestations of cerebral small vessel disease and are a major contributor to vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia. Although WMH have traditionally been attributed to chronic ischemia resulting from small vessel pathology, the biological mechanisms underlying their development and, more importantly, their progression remain incompletely understood. Recent advances in longitudinal neuroimaging, quantitative MRI, pathology, genetics, and physiological imaging have substantially expanded our understanding of WMH progression, making this an appropriate time to evaluate current concepts and synthesize emerging evidence. We review contemporary evidence regarding the biological processes implicated in WMH development and progression, including hypertension and vascular risk factors, acute ischemic injury, chronic hypoperfusion, blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction, endothelial activation and vascular inflammation, arterial stiffness, intracranial artery dolichoectasia (IADE), altered cerebral fluid dynamics and genetic susceptibility. Longitudinal studies demonstrate that WMH exhibit dynamic trajectories characterized by progression, stability, and partial regression, indicating that lesion evolution is not uniformly irreversible. Pathological and advanced neuroimaging studies show that WMH represent heterogeneous tissue injury involving demyelination, axonal loss, gliosis, interstitial fluid accumulation, and microvascular abnormalities. Hypertension and blood pressure variability are consistently associated with greater WMH burden and progression, whereas baseline WMH burden is the strongest predictor of future lesion expansion. Acute ischemic lesions detected by diffusion-weighted imaging contribute to, but account for only a minority of WMH progression. Longitudinal studies evaluating cerebral perfusion, BBB permeability, inflammation, arterial stiffness, IADE and cerebral fluid dynamics have yielded variable findings but, together with genetic evidence, support roles of BBB leakage, vascular inflammation, chronic hypoperfusion, arterial and extracellular-matrix remodeling, and impaired interstitial fluid clearance in WMH progression. Emerging evidence supports a paradigm in which WMH are viewed as a dynamic manifestation of progressive neurovascular dysfunction rather than the consequence of chronic ischemia alone. Current data suggest that early neurovascular injury evolves into a potentially self-reinforcing process characterized by persistent BBB disruption, vascular inflammation, chronic hypoperfusion, altered fluid dynamics, and recurrent ischemic injury, collectively contributes to WMH progression. Future multimodal longitudinal studies integrating cerebral hemodynamics, neurovascular function and intracranial arterial remodeling will be essential to understand WMH progression.

title: Mastering the Eye: Clinical Paradigm Shifts from Optical Restoration to Genomic Correction.
journal: Progress in retinal and eye research
abstract: Historically, the main operation for cataract was couching, and the interior of the living eye could not be examined until Hermann von Helmholtz introduced the ophthalmoscope in 1851. Since the mid-twentieth century, seven advances have reshaped ophthalmic care. Harold Ridley implanted the first intraocular lens in 1949, and the ophthalmologist Charles Kelman and the engineer Anton Banko developed phacoemulsification, reported in 1967. Robert Machemer performed the first pars plana vitrectomy in 1970, while David Huang and colleagues described optical coherence tomography in 1991. Endothelial keratoplasty, developed by Gerrit Melles and others between 1998 and 2006, replaced only the failing corneal endothelium instead of the full thickness of the cornea. Anti-VEGF therapy followed the purification of VEGF by Napoleone Ferrara and colleagues in 1989 and the approval of ranibizumab in 2006. Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery has spread since 2012, and in 2017 voretigene neparvovec became the first approved gene therapy for an inherited retinal disease. Five of these advances enabled a new type of intervention, whereas endothelial keratoplasty and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery made existing operations safer. For each advance we summarize the best available evidence of benefit to patients and its certainty, which is high for some, such as anti-VEGF therapy, and low for others, such as the effect of imaging on patient outcomes. Each advance created new burdens, from chronic injections to dependence on donor tissue, and routine adoption depended on manufacturing, regulation, cost, reimbursement, and health-system capacity.

title: Maternal high-fat diet and metformin treatment affect palatable diet preference and central reward system gene expression in rat offspring in a sex-specific manner.
abstract: Maternal metformin (MT) treatment improves the metabolic phenotype of high-fat (HF) diet-exposed offspring, but its effect on offspring's palatable food preference remains unclear. We assessed HF diet and sucrose preferences in adult offspring from Sprague-Dawley rat dams fed a control diet, an HF diet with or without MT treatment. Additionally, we measured the mRNA expression of sweet taste perception-related genes in taste buds and dopamine- and opioid-related genes in the central reward system. In adult males, maternal HF diet increased HF food preference and decreased dopamine-related gene expression in the reward system. Furthermore, maternal MT treatment decreased low-concentration sucrose preference, and reduced opioid-related gene expression in the reward system. Maternal HF diet elevated sweet taste perception-related gene expression in taste buds, while maternal MT treatment reversed these changes. In adult females, neither maternal HF diet nor MT treatment affected HF food preference. However, maternal HF diet decreased low-concentration sucrose preference and reduced the expression of sweet taste perception-related genes, while maternal MT treatment did not reverse it. At weaning, maternal MT treatment generally decreased dopamine- and opioid-related gene expression in the central reward system across both sexes. Notably, this early-life central reward transcriptional suppression persisted into adulthood in males but not in females. Our results indicate that maternal HF diet and MT treatment influence HF diet and low-concentration sucrose preferences in adult offspring in a sex-specific manner, which may be associated with altered gene expression in the central reward system and the peripheral taste perception pathways.

title: Systemic oxidative stress in patients with Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder and oxidative stress (OS) is believed to play a role in disease pathogenesis. However, reliable OS markers are lacking. In this study we aim to assess OS in AD by evaluating free thiols, which serve as key indicators of the systemic redox status. SCD (subjective cognitive decline), MCI (mild cognitive impairment), AD, and other dementias (Non-AD) were recruited. Comorbidity data were collected and free thiols were measured in plasma. Additionally, phosphorylated-Tau (pTau217), amyloid-beta ratio (Aβ42/40), Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (GFAP), and neurofilament light (NfL) levels were used to investigate correlation with free thiols. Further, associations between free thiols and disease severity in AD were calculated. Three hundred and ten patients were included (SCD 109, MCI 51, AD 125, Non-AD 25). Free thiols were significantly lower in AD compared to SCD and MCI (p<0.01). Free thiols correlated negatively with pTau217, NfL and GFAP, also within AD (p<0.01 for all). Additionally, free thiols significantly negatively correlated with Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA) scores (N=210, p<0.001). Multiple linear regression showed that type 2 diabetes and age were significant predictors for free thiols (B=1.01, β=0.266, p<0.001; B=-0.040, β=-0.273, p<0.001, respectively). After adjusting for these covariates, free thiols remained significantly lower in AD compared to SCD (p<0.05). Increased systemic OS, reflected by lower free thiols, is observed in plasma of AD patients, supporting a key role for OS in AD-pathophysiology and highlighting free thiols as potential therapeutic targets and possibly complementary biomarkers for clinical diagnostics.

title: Elastin-derived peptide VGVAPG induces redox-associated pro-inflammatory activation and early disease-associated microglia (DAM) molecular profile in a human microglia-neuron in vitro model involving NEU1/TLR4-related signaling.
abstract: The elastin-derived hexapeptide Val-Gly-Val-Ala-Pro-Gly (VGVAPG) exhibits well-documented biological activity; however, its role in brain inflammation remains insufficiently characterized. This is an important issue, as VGVAPG levels increase with age and have been implicated in processes contributing to neurodegeneration. The present study aimed to evaluate the ability of aging-related VGVAPG to activate human microglial (HMC3) cells in vitro and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Our results demonstrated no cytotoxic effect of VGVAPG. However, further analyses revealed NF-κB nuclear translocation, elevated ROS and •NO production, enhanced iNOS, and accumulation of NLRP3-containing vesicles in the cytoplasm, consistent with the peptide's pro-inflammatory potential. Additionally, activation of stress- and inflammation-related signaling pathways involving p38-MAPK, JNKs, and ERK1/2 was observed, accompanied by upregulation of NFKB1, IL1B, and TNFα mRNA. Using a transwell co-culture model of HMC3 and cholinergic-like neurons (differentiated SH-SY5Y), we observed potential DAMP-associated molecular changes involving HMGB1 and APP. Additionally, NEU1 siRNA-mediated knockdown in HMC3 cells, together with the observed NEU1/TLR4 colocalization, raises the possibility that NEU1 and TLR4 may be involved in the effects induced by VGVAPG. Moreover, VGVAPG induced alterations in early disease-associated microglia (DAM)-related protein profiles, including β2M, ITGAX, and ICAM1. Collectively, these findings identify VGVAPG as a candidate pro-neuroinflammatory matrikine in vitro and provide associative evidence for selected redox, NEU1-, TLR4-related, and early DAM-associated molecular changes. Further investigations employing advanced in vivo and translational models are warranted to validate these observations and to clarify the pathophysiological role of VGVAPG in the progression of neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Sex-divergent neurovascular and cognitive effects of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
abstract: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion is the leading risk factor for the development of vascular dementia and is associated with white matter damage and cognitive impairment. Here, we assessed sex differences in vascular and neural pathology and cognitive impairment in the asymmetric carotid arterial stenosis (ACAS) mouse model of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion. Thirty days of ACAS significantly reduced cerebral blood flow, increased microvascular permeability as evidenced by extravasation of IgG and fibrinogen into brain parenchyma, and impaired MCA vasodilation. ACAS also induced white matter damage in the hippocampus and corpus callosum, with greater damage in the corpus callosum of females compared to males. Spatial memory impairments on the Barnes maze were significantly greater in ACAS males than in females. Finally, miRNA analyses revealed upregulated angiogenic miRNA in the hippocampus and cortex in ACAS females and upregulated neuroinflammatory miRNA in the hippocampus and cortex in ACAS males. Together, these findings indicate that the ACAS model produces robust neuropathology and sex differences in spatial memory and miRNA profiles.

title: Risk Factors and Clinical Outcomes of Reocclusion after Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke: An Updated Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression.
journal: Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie
abstract: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined. Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions. Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced. Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.

title: Meta-Analytic Evidence of Clinical, Cognitive, Biological and Treatment Characteristics of Bipolar Spectrum Disorder in Children and Adolescents: Results From an Umbrella Review.
journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
abstract: To comprehensively synthesize the meta-analytic evidence regarding bipolar spectrum disorder (BSD) in children and adolescents. PRISMA-compliant umbrella review (PROSPERO:CRD420250651065) across multiple databases to identify meta-analyses involving children and adolescents with BSD. Literature search, screening, data extraction, and quality assessment (via AMSTAR-2) were performed independently. Findings were synthesized and grouped according to key clinical, cognitive, biological and treatment domains. Fifty-two meta-analyses were included (k=754, N=59,967, age=13.0 years, 44.8% female participants). Most reported symptoms were increased energy (79%, 95% confidence interval (CI)=61-93%), irritability (77%, 95%CI=64-88%), and mood lability (76%, 95%CI=55-92%). Psychiatric comorbidities were common, with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder being most frequent (53%, 95%CI=36-70%). Treatment delay was longer in children and adolescents than in adults with BSD (SMD=0.39, 95%CI=0.15-0.64). 26.2% (95%CI=24.4-28.0) of children and adolescents with BSD attempted suicide at least once, with higher risk vs. children and adolescents with depression (OR=1.59; 95%CI=1.24-2.05) and adult-BSD (OR=1.68, 95%CI=1.29-2.18). Compared to healthy controls (HCs), children and adolescents with BSD showed neurocognitive impairments. Abnormalities in neuroimaging markers were significant in children and adolescents with BSD vs. HCs, children and adolescents with depression and adult-BSD. Second-generation antipsychotics (SMD=0.68, 95%CI=0.51-0.86) and mood stabilizers (SMD=0.61, 95%CI=0.40-0.82) were superior for mania vs. placebo. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) was associated with improvements in manic and depressive symptoms. BSD in children and adolescents is linked to illness severity, cognitive deficits, and neuroimaging abnormalities, requiring integrated pharmacological and psychosocial interventions (e.g. CBT). SGAs effectively treat mania, but options for depression remain limited. More prognostic and long-term studies are needed.

title: Clinical and genetic correlates of a circadian subtype of depression in the Australian Genetics of Depression Study.
journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
abstract: Although commonly accepted depressive subtypes reflect phenotypic differences, there has been minimal progress in identification of discrete pathophysiological pathways, biomarkers or differential therapeutic approaches to effectively guide clinical management. To test the biological validity and clinical utility of a circadian subtype of depression on the basis of clinical course, differential medication response (self-reported) and genetic risk profile. Cross-sectional data were drawn from the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Participants were classified as having a 'circadian' or 'non-circadian' subtype of depression on the basis of meeting criteria for at least three binary circadian-associated features: social jetlag, seasonality, delayed sleep midpoint, evening chronotype, morning tiredness and hypersomnia. Clinical course characteristics were compared. Associations with response to commonly prescribed antidepressants and polygenic risk scores for mental disorders and sleep, circadian, metabolic and inflammatory traits were investigated using logistic regression models. A total of 2604 participants (23%; 80% female; mean age 37.87 ± 13.62 years) had a circadian subtype. They reported an earlier age at onset (P < 0.001), more severe clinical features including (hypo)manic-like and psychotic-like experiences, suicidality, psychological distress and somatic complaints (all P < 0.001), weight gain during depressive episodes (P < 0.001), poorer response to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (odds ratio 0.88 [95% CI 0.82, 0.94]) and serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors (odds ratio 0.89 [95% CI 0.83, 0.97]), and more side-effects compared with those with a non-circadian subtype. Having a circadian subtype was associated with higher polygenic risk scores for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (odds ratio 1.11 [95% CI 1.06, 1.17]), major depression (odds ratio 1.11 [95% CI 1.06, 1.16]), anxiety (odds ratio 1.10 [95% CI 1.04, 1.15]), bipolar disorder (odds ratio 1.09 [95% CI 1.04, 1.14]), body mass index (odds ratio 1.09 [95% CI 1.05, 1.14]), triglycerides (odds ratio 1.10 [95% CI 1.06, 1.16]), interleukin-6 (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.03, 1.13]), higher insulin resistance (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.04, 1.13]), later sleep midpoint (odds ratio 1.15 [95% CI 1.10, 1.21]), insomnia (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.03, 1.13]) and later chronotype (odds ratio 0.68 [95% CI 0.65, 0.71]). These findings support the face validity and potential clinical utility of a circadian subtype of depression as a clinical profile. Pending independent replication, investigation of its biology and predictive utility are warranted.

title: Maintaining Scientific Integrity: The Many Faces of Fraud.

Outcomes of Mindful Mood Balance for Moms, online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for perinatal depressive relapse prevention in the USA: a two-arm, single-blind, pragmatic randomised clinical trial.
abstract: Effective and accessible approaches to prevent depressive relapse and reduce symptoms are crucial for addressing the major public health problem of depression among perinatal women. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of Mindful Mood Balance (MMB) for Moms plus usual care (hereafter MMB for Moms)-a web-based mindfulness-based cognitive therapy programme customised for perinatal women-compared with usual care only, in reducing depressive relapse and symptoms. This single-blind, randomised clinical trial was done across the USA, in euthymic pregnant women with recurrent depression who were on recent or current antidepressant medication. Recruitment occurred from March 7, 2019, to July 8, 2020 (data collection was completed Sept 12, 2021). Participants were randomly assigned to MMB for Moms, or usual care. Primary outcomes were reduction in depressive relapse risk and symptom burden, assessed using the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview and Patient Health Questionaire-9, respectively, across the study period. Outcomes were assessed from baseline until 6-months postpartum in three phases (intervention, end of intervention to delivery, and postpartum). The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03623620, and is complete. Participants were recruited between March 7, 2019, and July 8, 2020. Data from 500 randomly assigned participants (mean age 32 years [SD 4·5] and mean 11·5 [2·8] weeks gestation), were analysed as the intention-to-treat sample. Of the 500 participants (249 assigned to MMB for Moms and 251 assigned to usual care), 383 [77%] provided assessment data at 3 months and 389 [78%] at 6 months postpartum. MMB for Moms had significantly lower risk of depressive relapse compared with usual care during the full trial period (up to 6 months postpartum): 81 (33%) of 249 participants assigned to MMB for Moms and 111 (44%) of 251 participants in usual care had depressive relapse (hazard ratio 0·74 [95% CI 0·56-0·99]; p=0·045; adjusted false discovery rate p=0·045). MMB for Moms was also associated with a significant reduction in depression symptom burden during the 12 week intervention phase (average decrease of 0·75 [SE 0·13] in the MMB for Moms group and 0·31 [0·13] in the usual care group) but not during the full trial period (average decrease of 0·61 [SE 0·18] in the MMB for Moms group and 0·54 [0·17] in the usual care group). MMB for Moms resulted in lower risk of relapse compared with usual care, and lower depression symptom burden during the intervention phase, potentially offering an effective non-pharmacological support option for depression relapse prevention during the perinatal period with positive implications for public health practice. US National Institutes of Health and US National Institute of Mental Health.

title: More than just accuracy: A pathway-level framework for implementing blood and digital biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease care.
abstract: Blood biomarkers are transforming Alzheimer's disease diagnostics by enabling a scalable, minimally invasive assessment of pathology. Food and Drug Administration clearances and European market certifications of different plasma tests mark a shift toward biological diagnosis in routine care. However, clinical implementation is not guided by diagnostic accuracy alone but will depend on improved patient-centered and pathway-level outcomes, including diagnostic confidence, the appropriate use of CSF and PET assessments, time to diagnosis, amyloid-targeting treatment eligibility assessment, and trial recruitment. Digital biomarkers may complement blood tests by providing repeated measures of cognition, speech, and mobility. Yet, their evidence base remains more heterogeneous regarding construct validity, supervision requirements, device dependence, adherence burden, cultural portability, interpretability, and regulatory classification. This review defines how combined blood-digital workflows could be evaluated beyond accuracy, including the context of use, downstream decisions, ethical aspects, governance, and post-market monitoring, ultimately aiming to translate biomarker innovation into meaningful benefits for patients and health systems.

title: Headache in Calcified Neurocysticercosis: Emerging Insights into an Inflammation-Driven Phenotype.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
abstract: Calcified neurocysticercosis (NCC), traditionally considered an inert marker of past infection, is increasingly recognized as a clinically meaningful condition associated with migraine-like headaches. Evidence from population-based cohorts, clinical series, and imaging studies consistently shows that individuals with calcified NCC have a higher prevalence and severity of headache than those without lesions. Prospective neuroimaging demonstrates that intermittent perilesional inflammation, including edema and blood-brain barrier disruption, can activate migraine-generating pathways, with calcitonin gene-related peptide-mediated trigeminovascular sensitization emerging as a key mechanism. These findings challenge the assumption that calcified lesions are clinically irrelevant and instead, support the concept of a distinct inflammation-driven headache phenotype. Recognizing this entity has important implications for diagnosis, counseling, and therapeutic decision-making, particularly in endemic regions where calcifications are common and often dismissed as incidental. Calcified NCC also provides a unique human model for understanding how focal neuroinflammation shapes headache susceptibility.

title: DAT-SPECT findings in POLR3A-related striatal variant: a case report and literature review.
abstract: The POLR3A striatal variant manifests with prominent extrapyramidal signs, ranging from early-onset dyskinetic syndromes to juvenile parkinsonism. This case report offers the first DAT SPECT evidence of nigrostriatal involvement, revealing significant reductions in striatal binding and decreased putamen-to-caudate ratios. These findings provide preliminary in vivo functional evidence of presynaptic dopaminergic involvement, offering a valuable biological correlate for the clinical phenotype.

title: The development and validation of the pre-sleep excitement-inducing activities scale.
abstract: Existing pre-sleep arousal measures emphasize distress-based symptoms, leaving positively valenced sources of activation, such as excitement-inducing evening activities, largely unassessed and a potential unmeasured contributor to sleep-onset difficulty. We developed and evaluated the Pre-Sleep Excitement-Inducing Activities Scale (PSEIA) to address this gap. A 34-item pool underwent expert review and cognitive debriefing. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was conducted in Phase 1 (n = 150). In an independent Phase 2 sample (n = 301), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) tested correlated three-factor, higher-order, and bifactor models. Internal consistency, two-week test-retest reliability (n = 150), and associations with the Pre-Sleep Arousal Scale (PSAS) were evaluated. Although parallel analysis suggested four factors, a more interpretable three-factor solution retained 18 items: Cognitive Stimulation, Informational Stimulation, and Recreational Stimulation. The correlated three-factor model showed CFI = .99, TLI = .99, RMSEA = .08, and SRMR = .06. The higher-order model had identical global fit; the bifactor model showed CFI = .99, TLI = .99, RMSEA = .07, and SRMR = .05. Total-score reliability was high (α = .92; ω = .95; ωH = .74), as was test-retest reliability (ICC = .93). The PSEIA correlated moderately with PSAS total score (r = .51, p < .001). The two shorter factors showed substantial overlap, and the three-item factor had marginal alpha (.69). The PSEIA provides an initial measure of activity-linked pre-sleep activation. Its reliable total score is supported by shared variance across factors, but subscale distinctiveness and clinical utility require further validation.

title: Sulfur-doped graphitic carbon nitride/cerium tungstate nanocomposites for ultrasensitive dopamine sensing in mouse striatal tissue.
abstract: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, the demand for rapid diagnostic tools for the highly specific and sensitive detection of disease-related biomarkers has increased significantly. Hybrid nanocomposite-modified disposable screen-printed electrodes have shown remarkable potential for the electrochemical biosensing of various biomarkers. This study reports the fabrication of a hybrid nanocomposite comprising sulfur-doped graphitic carbon nitride (S-g-C3N4) nanosheets integrated with two-dimensional cerium tungstate (CeW) for highly sensitive electrochemical dopamine detection. The synthesized S-g-C3N4@CeW hybrid nanocomposite was thoroughly characterized using field-emission scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, and electrochemical measurements. Electroanalytical performance was evaluated using differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) under optimized experimental conditions. The fabricated electrochemical sensor exhibited a wide linear concentration range for dopamine from 0.1 to 500 μM, with a low detection limit of 1.13 nM and high sensitivity of 151.69 μA μM-1 cm-2. Finally, the fabricated sensor was used for the ex-vivo determination of dopamine in Parkinson's disease-induced mouse striatum-tissue samples, achieving good accuracy with recovery rates of 92.0 to 101.4%. This study demonstrates a promising strategy for fabricating hybrid nanocomposite-modified disposable electrochemical sensors for neurotransmitter detection in animal-disease models.

title: Angioarchitectural Clues to Durable Endovascular Cure in High-Grade Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas.
Design, synthesis, and pharmacological evaluation of 7-substituted 1,2,4-triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine derivatives as novel antiepileptic lead candidates targeting Nav1.2 channels.
abstract: The limitations of current antiepileptic drugs, including drug resistance and adverse effects, necessitate the development of novel therapeutic agents with improved efficacy and safety. Herein, we describe the design, synthesis, and pharmacological evaluation of a series of novel 1,2,4-triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine derivatives. Through strategic modification at the C-7 position, we identified compound 5m as a highly potent anticonvulsant agent. In the pentylenetetrazole (PTZ) epilepsy model, 5m exhibited exceptional antiseizure activity (ED50 = 8.84 mg/kg) with a high protective index (PI > 14.80), demonstrating superior efficacy and safety profiles compared to valproate, carbamazepine, and phenobarbital. Notably, 5m showed no neurotoxicity at its maximum soluble concentration. Preliminary structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis at the C-7 position suggested that the trifluoromethanesulfonate substituent, the pyrimidine nitrogen atoms, and the ortho-fluoro substitution pattern on the phenyl ring are important for potent activity. Mechanism of action studies combining electrophysiological patch-clamp recordings and molecular docking simulations established Nav1.2 channels as a primary molecular target, with 5m exhibiting inhibitory activity against Nav1.2 channels (23% ± 17% inhibition at 10 μM) and forming key interactions with residues LEU329, LEU336, ASN388, GLN391, and ARG395, while showing no significant effect on GABAA receptors. Furthermore, in silico ADMET prediction confirmed that 5m possesses excellent drug-like properties, including favorable gastrointestinal absorption and blood-brain barrier permeability, with no predicted toxicity. In summary, compound 5m represents a promising novel antiepileptic lead candidate with high efficacy, low neurotoxicity, and a favorable drug-like profile, warranting further preclinical development.

title: Hemodynamic Effects of Interfacility Dexmedetomidine Infusions During Transport of Patients with Alpha-2-adrenergic Agonist Withdrawal.
journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
abstract: In the Philadelphia region, there has been an increase in the potency of illicit opioids as well as the addition of nonopioid adulterants. Currently, medetomidine, a veterinary anesthetic that acts as an alpha-2-adrenergic agonist, is a common adulterant in the illicit opioid supply, causing both unique overdose and withdrawal syndromes. Although opioid withdrawal alone is not deadly, with added adulterants, especially medetomidine, this is no longer the case. Dexmedetomidine is an alpha-2-adrenergic agonist frequently used for sedation in the emergency department and intensive care unit. Dexmedetomidine is also used off-label to treat the life-threatening withdrawal from alpha-2-agonists. This study describes the dosing and hemodynamic effects associated with the interfacility administration of dexmedetomidine in patients with alpha-2 adrenergic agonist withdrawal. Secondarily, we describe the safety of dexmedetomidine in this patient population. We conducted a retrospective case review of patients receiving dexmedetomidine infusions in the interfacility setting for presumed alpha-2-adrenergic agonist withdrawal. Demographic data, dosing, and vital signs were analyzed descriptively. Over a six-month period, of 217 cases identified, 182 contained complete hemodynamic data. The average age was 39.5 years, and 67% were male. The average transport time was 15.7 minutes (range, 5-40 minutes). The mean dexmedetomidine infusion rate was 1.32 (0.31) mcg/kg/hr. The average mean arterial pressure decreased from 122.1 mm Hg (21.7) at the time of initial patient contact to 118.3 mm Hg (21.7) (mean difference, 3.80; 95% CI, 1.96-5.64) at final patient interaction. Heart rate also showed a minimal change from 104.9 (23.7) to 103.6 (21.8) beats/min (mean 1.3; 95% CI, -0.48 to 3.08). No cases of severe hypotension or clinically significant bradycardia requiring intervention were documented (one-sided 95% CI, 0-1.7%). In this case series of patients, prehospital dexmedetomidine infusions to treat alpha-2-agonist withdrawal were associated with stable hemodynamics without significant bradycardia or hypotension. These findings support the safety of dexmedetomidine infusions for interfacility transport and provide a rationale for examining whether advanced life support clinicians can safely transport patients receiving dexmedetomidine infusions for this indication.

title: Prehospital Flumazenil: Five-Year Review of Use, Indications, Outcomes, and Adverse Events in Suspected Benzodiazepine Overdose.
journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
abstract: Historically, flumazenil was employed as both a diagnostic aid in unresponsive patients and as an antidote for suspected benzodiazepine overdose in both emergency departments and out-of-hospital settings. However, its prehospital application has been historically constrained by long-standing concerns regarding adverse events, leading many emergency medical service (EMS) systems to restrict or avoid its use. The use of flumazenil in the prehospital setting remains underreported in the literature, despite its inclusion in the treatment protocols of various EMS agencies. We conducted a descriptive analysis of the use of flumazenil by EMS in the out-of-hospital setting across the state of Kansas over a five-year period. We characterize the frequency, indications, patient outcomes, and associated adverse events of flumazenil administration, thereby contributing to a better understanding of its role, safety, and clinical relevance in prehospital care. We performed a retrospective observational cohort design to evaluate the use of flumazenil by EMS clinicians in the state of Kansas from January 2015-August 2020. Patient care reports documenting prehospital administration of flumazenil were obtained from the Kansas Board of EMS. Data extracted included demographics, indications, initial and subsequent Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores when available, clinical response, and the occurrence of adverse events. Our primary outcome measure was GCS improvement following administration, with secondary outcome measures including patterns and outcomes with flumazenil use in the prehospital setting, clinical response, and occurrence of adverse side effects. A total of 80 cases involving EMS administration of flumazenil were identified with 69 cases meeting inclusion criteria. No seizures or adverse events were associated with flumazenil use (0/69; 95% CI, 0-4.3%), even in administrations with possible contraindications. Of the 69 cases analyzed, 24 cases documented suspected benzodiazepine overdose, all of which documented neurologic improvement (24/24; 95% CI, 87.5-100%), with 17 receiving flumazenil alone and 7 with naloxone coadministration. In this small sample, no adverse events were noted with flumazenil administration in the prehospital setting. Flumazenil administration was commonly associated with documented improvement in GCS in suspected benzodiazepine overdose. These findings suggest that exclusion in EMS protocols based solely on concern for adverse events in the prehospital setting can be reconsidered. Further research is needed to better define its safety, efficacy, and clinical utility in this setting.

title: Intravenous Ketamine for Depressed and Suicidal Adolescents in the Emergency Department: A Randomized Double-Blind Trial.
journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
abstract: Adolescents frequently seek care in the emergency department (ED) for behavioral health emergencies. Due to national shortages in staffing, limited opportunities to begin treatment on site in most centers and, thus, the frequent default to elusive inpatient psychiatric beds as a means of stabilization, adolescents may spend prolonged amounts of time boarding in the ED, often without treatment. Ketamine is a rapid-acting antidepressant with emerging evidence in adults, but data are limited on its effectiveness in suicidal youth. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a single dose of intravenous (IV) ketamine on depression and suicidality scores compared to placebo in adolescents with treatment-resistant depression presenting to the ED with suicidal ideation.
