We conducted a two-arm randomized double-blind placebo controlled trial on a convenience sample of adolescents 12-17 years of age with treatment-resistant depression (trialed at least two antidepressants for at least four weeks each) who presented to the ED with suicidal ideation requiring psychiatric admission. Exclusion criteria included psychosis, substance abuse disorder, intoxication, developmental delay, aggressive behavior, and medical contraindications to ketamine. Subjects were randomized to receive a single dose of ketamine (0.2 mg/kg IV, maximum 35 mg) or saline placebo over two minutes. They completed the Beck Youth Inventory (BYI) and Suicidal Ideation Questionnaire (SIQ) at baseline and at 1 hour, 3 hours, 1 day, 3 days, and 7 days post-treatment. We compared groups with the Fisher exact and two-sided rank-sum tests. Our primary outcome measure was the proportion of subjects with a reduction of ≥ 50% on the BYI and SIQ within 3 hours after treatment. The 29 subjects (14 placebo, 15 ketamine) did not differ significantly in demographic and clinical characteristics. Despite reductions in BYI and SIQ in both groups, the proportions achieving ≥ 50% reductions did not differ significantly at 1 hour (SIQ: placebo, 0% vs ketamine 14.3 % [P = .48]; BYI Anxiety Inventory: placebo, 0% vs ketamine 21.4% [P = .22]; BYI Depression Inventory: placebo, 0% vs ketamine 15.4% [P = .22]). Differences at 3 hours were less pronounced. Adverse effects were more frequent in the ketamine group, most notably signs of dissociation (7% vs 60%, P = .004), with none after the 1-hour observation period. The ED offers an opportunity to deliver rapid-acting antidepressant treatment for suicidal adolescents. Although low-dose ketamine was not associated with greater reductions in depression or suicidality than placebo, this study demonstrated feasibility and highlights the need for larger studies to determine optimal ketamine dosing, route of administration, and implementation strategies in the ED setting.

title: Child Neurology: Neonatal Management of Tyrosine Hydroxylase Deficiency: How Early Is Early Enough?
abstract: Tyrosine hydroxylase deficiency is a rare, treatable, autosomal recessive disorder of monoamine neurotransmitter biosynthesis that typically presents in infancy or early childhood. Despite potential benefits of presymptomatic treatment with levodopa/carbidopa, prenatal or neonatal diagnosis remains extremely rare. We report 2 preterm neonates from unrelated families, both with known family history of tyrosine hydroxylase deficiency. After early diagnosis, levodopa/carbidopa therapy was initiated during the neonatal period. This proactive approach proved feasible and well tolerated, leading to early normalization of subtle motor abnormalities. These cases highlight the importance of early genetic diagnosis of this rare condition and the feasibility of levodopa/carbidopa treatment in neonates.

title: Recanalization After Acute Cervical Artery Dissection: A Multicenter International Study.
abstract: The rates and factors associated with complete recanalization after cervical artery dissection (CeAD) have not been comprehensively quantified in large cohorts. We sought to determine the 6-month rate of complete recanalization in CeAD, clinical and imaging factors associated with recanalization, and risk of recurrent ischemic stroke based on recanalization status. This was a planned subanalysis of the Antithrombotic Treatment for Stroke Prevention in Cervical Artery Dissection study, a multicenter retrospective cohort including patients with imaging-confirmed CeAD diagnosed between January 2015 and June 2022 at 63 sites worldwide. For this analysis, we included 1,095 patients with single-vessel CeAD causing stenosis at presentation who had available follow-up vascular imaging at 6 months after CeAD. The primary outcome was complete recanalization within 6 months after CeAD. Clinical and imaging variables, as well as recurrent stroke, were compared between patients with and those without complete recanalization. Factors independently associated with complete recanalization were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Time to complete recanalization was analyzed using an accelerated failure time Weibull model. Among 1,095 included patients (median age 45 years; 46.7% female), 634 (57.9%) achieved complete recanalization by 6 months. In multivariable analysis, each additional year of age was associated with lower odds of complete recanalization (odds ratio [OR] 0.97 per year; 95% CI 0.96-0.98; p < 0.001). Diabetes (OR 0.46; 95% CI 0.27-0.81; p = 0.006), active smoking (OR 0.69; 95% CI 0.50-0.95; p = 0.025), and complete occlusion at presentation (OR 0.44; 95% CI 0.32-0.59; p < 0.001) were independently associated with lower odds of complete recanalization. Complete occlusion at presentation was associated with both longer time to, and lower rates of, complete recanalization. We observed no effect of antithrombotic regimen (antiplatelet therapy vs anticoagulation) on complete recanalization. Incomplete recanalization was associated with a nonsignificant numerically higher proportion of recurrent stroke (5.4% vs 3.5%; p = 0.064). Almost 60% of patients with CeAD achieved complete vessel recanalization by 6 months. Older age, diabetes, smoking, and complete occlusion at presentation were independently associated with incomplete recanalization. Further study is required to determine whether these findings may help guide tailored imaging surveillance and secondary prevention strategies.

title: The Schematic Brain: The Neurophysiology of Behavioral Schemas.
journal: The Neuroscientist : a review journal bringing neurobiology, neurology and psychiatry
abstract: How does prior experience shape the way we interpret new situations, learn faster, and adapt when the world changes? These capacities depend on schemas: structured representations of relational knowledge that the brain builds through experience and reuses flexibly across contexts. Although schemas have long been central to theories of memory and cognition, their neural implementation is only now becoming accessible through advances in large-scale neural recordings, population-level analysis methods, and precise causal circuit tools. Here we review the emerging systems neuroscience of schemas, focusing on animal models where mechanistic dissection is feasible. We argue that schema formation, use, and updating are not discrete processes but reflect a continuous adaptive interplay between the strength of prior knowledge and the degree to which new information aligns with it. At the neural level, schemas appear to be encoded as structured low-dimensional population geometries distributed across hippocampal-prefrontal circuits, with distinct but interacting contributions from orbitofrontal cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, anterior cingulate cortex, and hippocampus. These representations actively shape perception, guide behavior, and reorganize when the environment demands it.

title: Plasticity in Human Brain Language Areas After Stroke: What Can the Right Hemisphere Do?
journal: The Neuroscientist : a review journal bringing neurobiology, neurology and psychiatry
abstract: Among the most devastating effects stroke can have on the lives of survivors and those around them are language production and comprehension impairments. The most notable of them - often given the joint diagnostic label of "aphasia" despite their heterogeneity and dissociability - are associated with damage to the brain's left hemisphere, which, in large part for this reason, is considered the "language-dominant" hemisphere. However, the right hemisphere's contribution to language should not be underestimated and may in fact be key to understanding the possibilities and limitations of neuroplasticity for supporting language recovery after stroke. Thus, in this review, we focus on the role of the right hemisphere in supporting human language function, in the neurologically healthy brain and after stroke. We discuss the remarkable capability of the right hemisphere to support normal language abilities after a large left-hemisphere stroke early in life, the more limited capacity for right-hemisphere language support after left-hemisphere stroke in adulthood, and potential interactions between typically left-hemisphere dominant "core" language functions with language functions typically thought to be right-hemisphere dominant, such as emotional prosody. We conclude by highlighting gaps in current knowledge and suggesting areas for future research.

title: Proenkephalin A and Heterogeneity of Hydrocortisone Treatment Effect in Septic Shock: A Post Hoc Analysis of the VANISH Trial.
abstract: Heterogeneity of treatment effect is thought to drive conflicting results for the benefits of corticosteroids in sepsis. Proenkephalin A (PENK) is a biomarker of renal function. Given the kidney's role in sepsis pathophysiology and corticosteroid metabolism, we hypothesized that baseline renal function, assessed using PENK, would be associated with hydrocortisone efficacy. A post hoc analysis of a double-blind, randomized clinical trial in septic shock (Effect of Early Vasopressin vs. Norepinephrine on Kidney Failure in Patients with Septic Shock [VANISH]). ICUs across the United Kingdom. One hundred seventy-three patients admitted to ICU with septic shock. Norepinephrine vs. vasopressin and hydrocortisone vs. placebo. PENK was measured in plasma, and patients were dichotomized using a PENK concentration above 89 pmol/L. PENK greater than or equal to 89 pmol/L was associated with 28-day mortality (odds ratio, 3.24; 95% CI, 1.62-6.74). We found no interaction between PENK and randomization to vasopressin or norepinephrine on outcome. However, there was a significant interaction between the PENK groups and hydrocortisone or placebo use in those patients who reached the maximum vasopressor threshold (n = 111) for kidney failure-free days (high PENK [≥ 89 pmol/L] placebo 26 [13-28], hydrocortisone 11 [0-26] and low PENK placebo 28 [15-28], hydrocortisone 28 [28-28]; p = 0.01). Patients with high PENK receiving hydrocortisone had the fewest kidney failure-free days. Although we found no significant interaction for 28-day mortality (p = 0.14), the patients with high PENK who received hydrocortisone had the highest mortality (high PENK hydrocortisone 50%, placebo 32% and low PENK hydrocortisone 14%, placebo 24%). This exploratory analysis identified a possible interaction between baseline PENK and hydrocortisone treatment on kidney failure-free days. These findings require validation in independent and prospective studies.

title: From Genes to Neural Circuits: Genetic and Systems Mechanisms of Ethanol Sensitivity and Tolerance in Drosophila melanogaster.
abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a complex neuropsychiatric disease shaped by genetic, environmental, and physiological factors. Over four decades, Drosophila melanogaster has emerged as a powerful model for dissecting the molecular and neural mechanisms underlying ethanol sensitivity, tolerance, preference, and consumption. Its conserved signaling pathways, sophisticated genetic toolkit, and robust behavioral assays have enabled discovery of genes and neural circuits governing alcohol responses across biological levels. This review summarizes major advances in the genetics and neurobiology of ethanol-related behaviors in Drosophila. Forward genetic screens identified conserved regulators of ethanol sensitivity and tolerance, including cAMP/PKA signaling components, ion channels, neurotransmitter receptors, cytoskeletal regulators, and neuropeptide pathways. Subsequent studies revealed distinct roles for the ellipsoid body, mushroom bodies, circadian neurons, and barrier glia in intoxication, tolerance, and reward. Epigenetic studies further established chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation as mechanisms of long-term behavioral plasticity, while systems genetics and genome-wide association studies highlighted the polygenic basis of natural variation in alcohol-related traits. Together, these findings advance an integrated view of ethanol action and provide a framework for understanding human AUD. Emerging approaches include single-cell and connectomics analyses, functional testing of human variants, and integration of systems genetics with circuit neuroscience.

title: Interfacial Polarization Dynamics of Nitrile Dipoles in Organic Synaptic Transistors for Acoustic Reservoir Computing.
abstract: Polar polymer interlayers have emerged as core functional layers in organic synaptic transistors (OSTs), enabling diverse neuromorphic behaviors through interfacial dipolar polarization and relaxation. However, the interfacial dipolar mechanisms governing memory window (ΔV) formation and modulation remain insufficiently understood. Here, polyacrylonitrile (PAN) is selected as a representative polar polymer interlayer to exploit nitrile (CN) dipolar relaxation for temporal acoustic reservoir computing (RC). It is found that the ΔV varies nonmonotonically with PAN concentration, suggesting a dipolar competition mechanism between interfacial polarization strength and dipole relaxation capability. Accordingly, dipolar relaxation underpins multiscale synaptic responses and fading memory for temporal RC. The device further exhibits stable and symmetric weight updates, with a low asymmetry ratio (AR) of 5.06% and cycle-to-cycle variations (CCVs) below 1%. Notably, the PAN-OST operates with an ultralow event energy of 50 aJ while maintaining a high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 50.47 dB. The PAN reservoir achieves 97.17% accuracy in spoken digit recognition and a maximum accuracy of 94.8% in the more challenging speech emotion recognition. Overall, this work establishes an interfacial polarization-driven pathway for energy-efficient neuromorphic computing and next-generation intelligent hardware.

title: Skeletal muscle fatigue resistance is differentially affected in 8-month-old male and female hAβ-KI mice.
abstract: Approximately 95% of Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnoses are sporadic onset, present after the age of 65, and arising from a combination of non-modifiable and modifiable factors. This underscores the potential to identify early systemic changes that may contribute to disease development. One factor may be skeletal muscle atrophy, which has been associated with cognitive decline, although the exact relationship between skeletal muscle and the brain is unknown. Furthermore, whether muscle atrophy begins prior to or after the onset of AD remains elusive. The humanized amyloid-beta knock-in mouse (hAβ-KI) exhibits age-related cognitive decline, insoluble Aβ accumulation, inflammation and microglial activation, making it a useful model of sporadic AD. However, characterization of skeletal muscle changes with aging has yet to be examined. Here, we assess skeletal muscle form and function of the hAβ-KI mouse at 8 and 15 months of age, before and after onset of cognitive decline, through assessment of whole-body lean mass percentage, isolated muscle contraction of the extensor digitorum longus (EDL) and soleus muscle, and fiber type analysis of male and female mice. Whole-body lean mass declined over time in all mice; however, only male hAβ-KI mice had a significant change in body mass and lean mass over the study. At 8-months-old, the isolated EDL of male hAβ-KI mice fatigued faster than the WT mice, but there were no differences at 15 months-old nor fiber type composition at either age. Alternatively, the isolated EDL and soleus of 8-month-old hAβ-KI female mice fatigued slower compared to the WT mice, and there were no differences at 15 months nor fiber type composition at either age. This preliminary characterization work suggests sex-dependent differences in isolated muscle fatigue prior to cognitive decline in the hAβ-KI mouse model of sporadic AD.

title: Delivering a high-dose walking booster program after stroke: a multimethod study of therapists' beliefs and experiences nested within a randomized trial.
abstract: High-dose motor training is rarely implemented later after stroke. This study explored intervention therapists' beliefs and experiences delivering a high-dose walking booster program (HiWalk) within a Phase II trial. The objectives of this study were to (i) describe the beliefs intervention therapists held about a high-dose walking booster program prior to delivery, (ii) report facilitators and barriers to delivery, and (iii) to describe the strategies intervention therapists used to maintain training intensity during the program. A multimethod design examined intervention therapists' perspectives of delivering a high-dose walking booster program to stroke survivors who were more than 6-months post-stroke. Pre-program surveys assessed beliefs about high-dose motor training. Observational audits evaluated program delivery. Semi-structured interviews, informed by the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF), identified facilitators and barriers to program delivery. Survey and observational audit data were descriptively analyzed, and qualitative data were analyzed thematically. The HiWalk Trial was registered on January 10, 2023 (registration number ACTRN12623000316606). All therapists who delivered the HiWalk program (n = 6) participated. Before delivery, intervention therapists believed high-dose training was important (98.5/100, SD 2.5) but were less confident that stroke survivors could complete 3 hours of training per day (74.8/100, SD 25.8). Audit observations indicated that, on average, observed intervention sessions met protocol expectations. Key facilitators included training (TDF Skills), team support (TDF Social Influences), and resources (TDF Environmental Context and Resources). Barriers were beliefs about stroke survivor capability (TDF Beliefs about Capabilities) and resource limitations (TDF Environmental Context and Resources). Intervention therapists can deliver a high-dose walking booster program within a clinical trial when supported by training, resources, and team collaboration. Findings inform future trial design and clinical practice translation.

title: Using 360-video to investigate visual exploratory activity in 7v7 and 9v9 sided games in women's soccer.
abstract: Immersive technology such as 360-video offers opportunities to analyse visual exploratory activity (VEA) under varying task constraints in controlled experimental settings. The study aimed to investigate the effect of pitch location and sided‑game format on VEA and verbal action responses in 360-video. Nineteen sub-elite female soccer players (21 ± 4 years) viewed 40 soccer videos in a head-mounted display. Footage was recorded using a stationary GoPro 360 Max camera at eye height in defensive and attacking central midfield locations. VEA was measured as the number of "scans" away from the ball across 32 analysed trials. Upon receiving a pass in 360-video, participants simulated and verbalised an action to continue play. A 2 × 2 repeated‑measures ANOVA showed a significant main effect of pitch location (p = 0.016), with higher scan frequencies in defensive (0.31 ± 0.15 scans/s) than attacking midfield (0.29 ± 0.15 scans/s), with no significant effect of sided‑game or interaction effect (p > 0.05). Findings demonstrate players had significantly higher scan frequencies in defensive central midfield compared with attacking central midfield, with the most verbal actions per trial in the 9v9 attacking midfield condition. Future research should assess agreement between VEA measured in 360-video and on-field activities.

title: EXPRESS: Synaptic density PET mediates the relationship between Alzheimer's disease pathology and cognitive performance.
journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
abstract: Synaptic loss is one of the strongest post-mortem predictors of Alzheimer's disease (AD) severity and may impact how pathology affects cognition. This study compared regional [11C]UCB-J synaptic density across the AD continuum and evaluated the extent to which synaptic density mediates relationships between AD biomarkers. Seventy-two participants completed PET scans, MRIs, and cognitive testing. Participants were categorized into subgroups representing typical AD progression. Regional synaptic density was compared across subgroups and pathological variables. Standard mediation and moderated mediation analyses were performed using amyloid and tau as predictors/moderators and MoCA score as outcome. The amyloid+/tau+/impaired subgroup showed lower synaptic density than controls, particularly for transverse temporal, inferior parietal, and hippocampal regions (Cohen's d=1.60, 1.57, 1.50). Hippocampal synaptic density had the strongest associations with tau (β=-0.473); transverse temporal synaptic density had the strongest association with amyloid (β=-0.543) and age (β=-0.614). Eight of twelve assessed brain regions demonstrated significant indirect effects across mediation frameworks. The inferior parietal lobe showed the largest mediation for amyloid (45.3%) and tau (28.9%). These findings support the hypothesis that synaptic loss is a primary mechanism contributing to clinical AD and suggest that synaptic density imaging can provide complementary information to the existing AD framework.

title: The association of particulate matter 2.5 exposure with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults and the potential modification by lifestyle and socioeconomic status.
journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
abstract: To examine PM2.5 exposure associations with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, and evaluate modifying effects of lifestyle and socioeconomic status (SES). We analyzed 10,659 participants from CHARLS using PM2.5 data from Dalhousie University. Frailty was assessed via a deficit accumulation index. Group-based trajectory modelling (GBTM) identified frailty trajectories; ordered logistic regression estimated associations and effect modifications. Three trajectories emerged: "Stable low" (63.95%), "Increased to frailty" (29.00%), and "Continuously worsening" (7.05%). Each 10 μg/m³ PM2.5 increase raised odds of Trajectories 2 and 3 by 15.2% and 12.3%, respectively. Higher SES attenuated PM2.5 effects (RERI=-0.067), while unhealthy sleep duration amplified them (RERI=0.163). PM2.5 exposure is associated with deteriorating frailty trajectories. Higher SES exerts an antagonistic effect, whereas unhealthy sleep duration has a synergistic effect on PM2.5-related frailty progression.

title: Maternal Factors Modifying the Link Between Genetic Risk for Autism and Developmental Milestones.
journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part B, Neuropsychiatric genetics : the official publication of the International Society of Psychiatric Genetics
abstract: Although common genetic liability-quantified through polygenic risk scores (PRS)-accounts for substantial variance in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) liability, how prenatal environmental exposures interact with genetic predisposition to shape developmental outcomes remains poorly understood. Using the data from Autism Genetic Resource Exchange (AGRE), we examined whether maternal prenatal factors moderate the association between ASD PRS and developmental outcomes, including language delay, motor delay, and core ASD traits. In exploratory gene-environment interaction analyses, amniocentesis was a candidate positive moderator of the association between PRS and both language and motor delay, such that higher polygenic liability was associated with a greater likelihood of these delays among prenatally exposed children. First-trimester vaginal bleeding showed a similar positive interaction estimate for motor delay. Maternal use of over-the-counter (OTC) medications during pregnancy-predominantly acetaminophen, reported by 59.9% of OTC users-was associated with an inverse interaction estimate, corresponding to a decreased association between polygenic liability and language delay among exposed children. These observations suggest that several prenatal factors may modify the association between common genetic liability and developmental outcomes among autistic children and should be considered hypothesis-generating until replicated in larger, population-based cohorts. Replication in independent samples, together with analyses that address selection and confounding, will be required before these candidate gene-environment interactions can be interpreted as reflecting specific developmental mechanisms.

title: Whole-blood transcriptomic findings in emergency department patients with suspected cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome: a pilot study.
abstract: Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome (CHS) is a paradoxical and increasingly prevalent disorder characterized by recurrent vomiting in people with chronic cannabis use. Despite its growing clinical impact, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Genome-wide RNA sequencing was used to characterize transcriptomic differences and identify potential pathways involved in CHS pathogenesis. In this pilot study, whole blood RNA sequencing was performed on 7 patients with suspected CHS and 7 matched controls. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified, annotated and analyzed by automated and manual analysis. RNA sequences were further analyzed by digital isotyping for HLA Class I and II allele usage. Suspected CHS was associated with marked activation of the adaptive immune system, including upregulation of B-cell related immunoglobin transcripts and altered expression of T cell, monocyte, and neutrophil-related transcripts. DEGs also suggested increased matrix degradation, and reduced adhesion and protease inhibitor transcripts. Digital HLA isotyping revealed increased MHC Class I expression, Class II allele restriction, and down-regulation of IgE receptor transcripts, a known response to elevated IgE levels in allergic hypersensitivity. Together, these preliminary findings identify immune-related signals in ED patients with suspected CHS, and lay the groundwork for future studies with larger, prospectively phenotyped cohorts to identify biomarkers, clarify immune triggers, and develop targeted therapies.

title: Capsaicin suppresses microglial inflammation through TRPV1-SSR4 interaction.
abstract: Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of microglial response during neuroinflammation, a key pathological feature of various neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease. Capsaicin, the primary pungent component in chili peppers, executes its anti-inflammatory properties as a TRPV1 agonist. Although the mechanism of TRPV1 channel activation and signal transduction by capsaicin has been extensively studied, the protein-protein interaction-based mechanisms by which TRPV1 modulates microglial inflammatory responses in the context of neurodegeneration remains unclear. We used a lipopolysaccharide-induced acute neuroinflammation model to examine the effects of TRPV1 activation and pharmacological blockade of TRPV1 channel gating on microglial inflammatory responses. Proximity labeling-based proteomics, bioluminescence resonance energy transfer, and NanoLuc Binary Technology were used to identify and characterize TRPV1-interacting proteins. Signal sequence receptor subunit 4 (SSR4) knockdown and forced interaction between TRPV1 and SSR4 were performed to assess the functional contribution of the TRPV1-SSR4 interaction. Structural modeling, BRET-based domain mapping, and colocalization analyses were further used to examine the molecular and subcellular features of SSR4 recruitment by TRPV1. In the neuroinflammatory model, the TRPV1 agonist capsaicin attenuated pro-inflammatory cytokine production, neuronal apoptosis, microgliosis, and microglial soma enlargement in a TRPV1-dependent manner. Notably, pharmacological blockade of TRPV1 channel gating by capsazepine did not abolish the anti-inflammatory action of capsaicin, suggesting an alternative mechanism of action beyond the canonical ligand-gated Ca2⁺ influx. Screening of TRPV1 prey proteins and validation strategy identified SSR4 as a capsaicin-responsive, TRPV1-associated protein. SSR4 knockdown in microglia significantly diminished the suppression of inflammatory responses caused by TRPV1 activation. Conversely, forced interaction between TRPV1 and SSR4 partially mimicked the anti-inflammatory effects of TRPV1 activation. Further structural and cellular analyses suggested that the transmembrane region of TRPV1 supports SSR4 recruitment. Our findings suggest that capsaicin suppresses microglial inflammation mediated by the TRPV1-SSR4 interaction, providing new insights into the chemical biology basis of TRPV1 interoceptive signaling and potential applications of natural TRPV1 agonists for modifying therapy of neuroinflammation-associated neurodegeneration.

title: Investigating long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) HOTAIR expression changes in ischemic stroke patients.
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS), a leading global health problem, is caused by interrupted blood flow in the brain, often due to clotting or artery constriction. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), particularly HOX transcript antisense intergenic RNA (HOTAIR), are pivotal in stroke pathophysiology. This study focused on the expression levels of HOTAIR lncRNA in ischemic stroke patients. This comparative cross-sectional study with 100 participants: 50 IS patients and 50 patients without IS serving as controls. The study gathered demographic data, disease specifics, and medication history. Blood samples were analyzed for HOTAIR lncRNA expression levels. This study showed significantly higher expression levels of HOTAIR lncRNA among IS patients compared to the control group (5.73 ± 0.75 vs. 2.35 ± 0.29; P < 0.001), with an average increase of 3.19 units compared to the control group (P < 0.001) after adjusting the independent variables. Additionally, participants with hypertension had an average increase of 0.36 units in of HOTAIR lncRNA expression compared to the control group (P = 0.041). Our study found that HOTAIR lncRNA levels are significantly higher in IS patients and may be associated with a history of hypertension. diseases. This suggests that HOTAIR lncRNA could be a useful biomarker for stroke and related conditions.

title: Motor network neurophysiological (TMS-EEG) markers as predictors of outcomes of ventriculoperitoneal shunt sustained for over a year in normal pressure hydrocephalus.
journal: Fluids and barriers of the CNS
abstract: Current practice for normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) relies on clinical presentation, imaging, and various clinical procedures to determine the need for neurosurgical intervention, specifically the installation of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VPS). This study aimed to evaluate the utility of a TMS-evoked potential (TEP)-based assessment (Delphi-MD) for predicting sustained response (over one year) to VPS, serving as an ancillary test to the cerebrospinal fluid tap test (CTT). Forty-one patients with possible iNPH underwent Delphi-MD evaluation of wave form adherence (WFA), a composite measure assessing how closely their TEPs resembled an ideal benchmark TEP. Of these, 18 patients received VPS treatment following a multidisciplinary team decision based on standard practice, blinded to the TEP results. Response to the intervention was evaluated over a period of more than one year using the clinical global impression of change (CGIC) scale, in addition to assessments with a 10-meter timed up and go test and the modified Rankin scale. Responders had higher M1L WFA values at baseline (prior to VPS) than non-responders (median 0.51 [95% CI 0.36-0.76], median 0.14 [95% CI -0.02-0.38], respectively p = 0.012). M1L WFA was successful in distinguishing responders (11/18) from non-responders (7/18) with an ROC-AUC of 0.935 [bootstrap 95% CI 0.792-1.00], p < 0.0001. M1L WFA cutoff was established with LOOCV and produced 90.9% sensitivity, 85.7% specificity and 88.9% accuracy. In contrast the CTT result was unsuccessful in predicting shunt responsiveness. This study indicates that higher M1L WFA obtained through Delphi-MD (TMS-EEG), signifies better preservation and functional integrity of the motor network in patients with probable iNPH that had a sustained response to VPS than those that did not. Given replication of results in future independent cohorts, Delphi-MD shows promise as an objective, accurate, and accessible ancillary screening tool for iNPH candidates, prior to referral for VPS treatment. Registration number: MOH_2021-12-08_010449. Registration date: 11.09.2021. https://clinicaltrial.health.gov.il/clinicaltrials/?sort=experimentapproveddate_tdt+desc&page=1&searchQuery=MOH_2021-12-08_010449 .

title: Comprehensive behavioral phenotyping of male Sulf1-deficient mice reveals reduced locomotor activity, altered forelimb gait, and reduced prepulse inhibition.
abstract: Sulfatase 1 (Sulf1) is an extracellular sulfatase that regulates multiple signaling pathways by removing 6-O-sulfate from heparan sulfate. Although Sulf1 has established roles in development and cancer, its functions in the adult brain remain incompletely characterized. Recently we reported that Sulf1 is expressed in the nucleus accumbens, overlapping with dopamine D1 and D2 receptors, and that Sulf1 knockout (KO) mice showed altered reward and aversion learning. However, given that Sulf1 is expressed in many other brain regions, including the prefrontal cortex, midline thalamic nuclei, etc., Sulf1 may have unknown brain functions. To explore the Sulf1 functions across a broad range of contexts, we here perform a comprehensive behavioral analysis of male Sulf1 KO mice, together with a re-analysis of the original data in which the false discovery rate (FDR) was controlled within defined groups of tests. Sulf1 KO mice traveled less than wild-type (WT) mice in the open field test, and this reduction was reproduced in an independent cohort. Gait analysis on a treadmill revealed a redistribution of the forelimb stance phase, with a larger proportion spent braking and a smaller proportion spent propelling, together with an increased absolute paw angle; these forelimb changes were reproduced in 2 independent cohorts and at 2 treadmill speeds. Distance traveled was also reduced in a three-chamber apparatus and, before drug injection, at nominal significance in the home cage. Sulf1 KO mice showed larger acoustic startle responses and reduced prepulse inhibition (PPI); the reduction in PPI was observed in all 5 drug-free or saline-treated sessions conducted in 2 independent cohorts and was also observed after haloperidol (0.3 or 1 mg/kg) and, at nominal significance, after clozapine (3 mg/kg) treatment. The locomotor, vertical, and stereotypic responses to methamphetamine were attenuated in Sulf1 KO mice, with nominally significant drug × genotype interactions. Increased baseline-subtracted contextual freezing provides a promising lead for further confirmation. Taken together, adult male Sulf1 KO mice exhibit alterations in locomotor output, forelimb gait, and sensorimotor gating, implicating that Sulf1 deficiency leads to a wide range of neurobehavioral abnormalities.

title: ABCD-Trial: study protocol for a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in patients with Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis for the evaluation of efficacy and safety of B-Cell Depletion with rituximab (ABCD).
abstract: The exact disease-causing mechanisms in ALS remain incompletely understood. A possible cause is inflammation of neurons. Compared to other neurodegenerative diseases, neuroinflammation is pronounced in ALS, presumably leading to disease progression and neuronal death. Patients with ALS can have neuronal autoantibodies and most notably antibody-producing cells in the cerebrospinal fluid. The CD20-binding therapeutic antibody rituximab targets these antibody-producing B-cells. Rituximab is a medication commonly used in neurology. Single patients with ALS have already been treated with rituximab, which was well tolerated. We therefore want to evaluate safety and efficacy of a treatment with rituximab in ALS patients in a double-blind placebo-controlled trial. With this trial we aim for slower disease progression and unveiling disease-causing mechanisms in ALS. A total of 52 male and female patients older than 18 years with active sporadic ALS and disease duration of less than 24 months who are on a stable dose of riluzole (50 mg BID) should be included. Patients requiring assisted ventilation of any kind or have a known intolerance to the study medication rituximab are excluded. The study medication rituximab or placebo should be administered over a period of 52 weeks at 4 distinct time points, followed by a follow-up period of 79 weeks with 4 visits. Treatment efficacy should be evaluated using the ALS functioning scale ALSFRS-R-SE at every study visit (except safety visits). Safety will be assessed through regular laboratory analyses, adverse event (AE) and serious adverse event (SAE) monitoring, and CD20+ B-cell kinetics. The primary endpoint is the change in the ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R-SE) from baseline to week 79. Trial sites will be at Charité/DZNE Berlin and DZNE Bonn. ALS is a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disease with limited treatment options. Recent preclinical in vivo studies suggest that B-cell-mediated autoimmunity contributes to disease progression. This trial will evaluate whether rituximab, which specifically depletes CD20+ B-cells, can slow ALS progression and provide insights into disease mechanisms. The trial was registered in the German WHO-recognized primary register Deutsches Register Klinische Studien DRKS (German Clinical Trials Register) on 3/07/2023 under registration number DRKS00030948.

title: Aging-enhanced accumulation of fibroblasts excludes oligodendrocytes in demyelinated lesions.
abstract: Fibroblast dysregulation contributes to pathological fibrosis and aberrant repair. Emerging evidence suggest that fibroblasts accumulate in lesions following central nervous system injury, but whether and how they influence oligodendrocyte repair responses, including in aging, is uncertain. Here we report that fibroblasts accumulate in the parenchyma of spinal cord white matter lesions of 6 - 10 week old young mice after lysolecithin-induced demyelination. This was first observed through immunofluorescence microscopy that employed several markers attributed to fibroblasts, including platelet-derived growth factor-β, collagen type 1α1, α-smooth muscle actin, periostin and fibronectin; and by the use of platelet-derived growth factor-β TdTomato reporter transgenic mice. Single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics of lysolecithin lesions established the presence of fibroblasts in lysolecithin lesions and delineated them from closely related pericytes. CellChat ligand - receptor analyses highlight fibroblasts in the lysolecithin environment as a major source of input of signals for microglia/macrophages and oligodendrocyte precursor cells, with numerous reciprocal interactions. The infiltration of fibroblasts was promoted by microglia/macrophages, as anticipated by their temporal representation in lysolecithin lesions, and by tissue culture experiments where the migration of fibroblasts was enhanced by macrophages. Of particular relevance to spontaneous regenerative events in lysolecithin demyelination, areas of fibroblast accumulation were devoid of oligodendrocyte precursor cells. In tissue culture, oligodendrocyte precursor cells were excluded from fibroblast domains. Moreover, fibroblast accumulation after lysolecithin injury was enhanced with increasing age, a known detriment to the capacity to remyelinate after injury, and exclusion of oligodendrocyte precursor cells from fibroblast areas of 48-52 week mice exceeds that occurring in younger 6-10 weeks animals. Finally, by mining a publicly available single-nucleus RNA database of multiple sclerosis, we found fibroblasts in the edge of chronic active and chronic inactive lesions and in lesion core, and fewer in periplaque or normal white matter. We identified several communication networks between fibroblasts, microglia/macrophages and oligodendrocyte precursor cells in these MS lesions. Our collective results demonstrate a role of fibroblasts in demyelination-associated neuropathology, which is exacerbated by aging, and highlight the importance of regulating fibroblasts to promote effective CNS repair.

title: StitchR-based dual-AAV delivery strategies enable efficient transduction of defined neural cell populations.
abstract: Dual adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector reconstitution has become an indispensable technique for delivering large genes in neuroscience and gene therapy. A novel technology termed StitchR addresses the challenge of low efficiency in dual-AAV reconstruction, yet related tools enabling targeted gene delivery to specific neural cell populations remain insufficiently developed. Herein, we developed four StitchR-based dual-viral reconstitution strategies by combining high-efficiency AAV serotypes with neuron- or glia-specific promoters. Specifically, the AAV11-hSyn-driven StitchR strategy achieved specific transduction of local neurons and their upstream projection neurons (≥ 94.44% specificity); the AAV11-GfaABC1D-driven strategy realized astrocyte-specific transduction (approximately 98.25% specificity); and the AAV11-mIBA1-driven strategy enabled microglia-specific transduction (100% specificity). Furthermore, by incorporating the blood-brain barrier (BBB)-penetrating AAVhu.32-PLUS into the hSyn-driven system, we established a modified strategy that allows brain-wide neuronal transduction. Finally, we confirmed that the StitchR-based dual-viral reconstitution strategy can achieve efficient functional reconstitution of large transgenes in neural cells. Collectively, these dual-AAV delivery strategies expand the valuable AAV toolbox and offer crucial technical support for targeted delivery of large transgenes to defined neural cell populations, holding great significance for basic neuroscience research and potential therapeutic applications.

title: Metabolic plasticity underlies ferroptosis resistance driven by mutant p53 in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by late diagnosis, rapid progression, and resistance to conventional therapies. Mutations in the tumor suppressor gene TP53 are prevalent in this cancer and have been associated with gain-of-function activities that promote tumor survival. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, represents a potential therapeutic vulnerability. However, the influence of mutant p53 on ferroptosis susceptibility remains poorly understood. We employed isogenic pancreatic cancer cell models, including CRISPR-Cas9-mediated TP53 Knockout (TP53-KO) and transient overexpression of common mutant TP53 variants, to examine ferroptosis sensitivity. Cell viability, reactive oxygen species accumulation, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial integrity, and metabolic profiling were assessed following treatment with ferroptosis inducers. Transcriptional changes were analysed by RNA sequencing, and functional contributions of glycolysis and mitochondrial respiration were evaluated using metabolic flux assays. Pharmacological reactivation of wild-type p53 was tested in combination with ferroptosis inducers in vitro and in orthotopic murine models. Deletion of mutant TP53 sensitized pancreatic cancer cells to ferroptosis, accompanied by increased oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation and mitochondrial dysfunction. Mutant TP53 expression preserved mitochondrial integrity and sustained bioenergetic flexibility under ferroptotic stress. Transcriptomic analyses revealed a multi-layered adaptive program, including upregulation of antioxidant and metabolic genes, and activation of PI3K-AKT signaling, which is associated to a selective glycolytic shift to maintain ATP levels. Functional modulation confirmed that glucose supplementation enhanced, whereas glycolytic inhibition impaired, survival under ferroptotic conditions in mutant TP53-expressing cells, but not in TP53-KO cells. Pharmacological reactivation of wild-type p53 disrupted this adaptive network, abrogating glycolytic reprogramming and significantly increasing ferroptotic cell death both in vitro and in vivo. Mutant p53 orchestrates transcriptional and metabolic plasticity that confers ferroptosis resistance in pancreatic cancer. Reactivating wild-type p53 in combination with ferroptosis induction overcomes this resistance, highlighting a therapeutically actionable vulnerability and supporting the development of combinatorial strategies for this aggressive malignancy.

title: Cost-effectiveness of iStent-based trabecular micro-bypass stenting combined with cataract surgery in mild-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma: a systematic review of analytic perspectives and time horizons.
journal: Cost effectiveness and resource allocation : C/E
abstract: Glaucoma remains a major cause of irreversible blindness and was estimated to affect 64.3 million people worldwide in 2013. Despite growing clinical use of minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS), reimbursement and uptake remain constrained by uncertainty about long-term cost-effectiveness. iStent-based trabecular micro-bypass implantation is commonly performed at the time of cataract surgery in patients with mild-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma, yet its economic value has not been synthesised systematically across healthcare systems. To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of iStent trabecular micro-bypass implantation performed concurrently with cataract surgery for mild-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma, and to examine how the analytic perspective and time horizon adopted in the underlying models relate to the decision the evidence is intended to inform. A systematic review was performed of published model-based economic evaluations. Eligible studies used a formal decision-analytic model, reported quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and evaluated an iStent device implanted concurrently with cataract surgery. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched on 27 July 2026 without date, language or publication-type restriction. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), QALYs, analytic perspectives, time horizons, discount rates and probabilistic results were extracted with a page reference for each value. Reporting was appraised item-by-item against CHEERS 2022. Findings were synthesised narratively; no quantitative pooling was attempted. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020. Of 418 records identified and 293 after de-duplication, eight economic evaluations from eight countries met the eligibility criteria. All eight compared the device added to cataract surgery against cataract surgery alone; seven used a cohort Markov model and one an individual-patient microsimulation. Six adopted a payer or health-system perspective and two a societal perspective; five used a lifetime horizon, one 35 years and two 15 years. No evaluation adopted a provider perspective or a base-case horizon shorter than 15 years. All eight reported a favourable base-case result in the mild-to-moderate target population: reported ratios included €1,154 per QALY in France, €12,676 in Spain, €13,037 in Italy, €10,955 to €15,673 in Germany, JPY 1,430,647 in Japan and A$2,430 in Australia, together with two instances of dominance. Six of the eight were funded by the device manufacturer. Incremental QALY gains were small throughout, between approximately 0.005 and 0.17, so the reported ratios are highly sensitive to small changes in the denominator. One study did not report a price year and for a second it could not be verified; no study reported a pre-specified health economic analysis plan, and none modelled long-term structural change in medication prices, prescribing practice or competing alternatives. The included peer-reviewed models generally project that adding an iStent-family device to cataract surgery can be cost-effective over long horizons. That projection depends on sustained medication reduction, on extrapolated glaucoma progression and on local device and treatment costs. Direct evidence that the modelled long-term clinical benefit is realised in practice and offsets the acquisition cost remains limited: the evidence base is small, concentrated in industry-funded analyses of a single device family drawing largely on the same two-year pivotal trial, and built on incremental QALY gains close to zero. All included evaluations adopt a payer, health-system or societal perspective over 15 years or longer, and none addresses whether the marginal cost of adding a stent to an already-scheduled cataract procedure is justified within an annual operating budget. This is a gap in the included QALY-based cost-utility literature; the review was not designed to identify provider-perspective budget-impact analyses outside these eligibility criteria. Not applicable. This study is a systematic review of published economicevaluations; no clinical trial registration was required. The review was not registeredprospectively in PROSPERO.

title: Non-suicidal self-injury and digital ostracism: a novel smartphone-based paradigm capturing real-time responses to social media exclusion.
journal: Borderline personality disorder and emotion dysregulation
abstract: Ostracism on social media is a common and emotionally salient stressor. However, its moment-to-moment psychological and behavioral consequences, remain poorly understood in individuals with Non-Suicidal Self-Injury (NSSI) and Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD). Using an Instagram-mimicking smartphone platform (Socializapp) coupled with Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA), we examined responses to experimentally manipulated peer feedback across 7 days in three groups: healthy Controls (HC; n = 20), NSSI without BPD (NSSI; n = 18), and comorbid BPD+NSSI (n = 17). Participants were exposed to Inclusion, Partial Exclusion, and Exclusion conditions. Linear and generalized linear mixed-effects models tested within-person effects on perceived exclusion and approval, affective reactivity, objective engagement (Likes and Comments) and NSSI urges, with borderline traits (BPQ) modeled dimensionally. Compliance was high, supporting feasibility. The manipulation was perceived as intended, with perceived exclusion increasing and perceived approval decreasing stepwise from Inclusion to Partial and Full Exclusion across participants. Exclusion also increased negative affect, reduced positive affect, and suppressed effortful interaction (fewer comments). In exploratory analyses, Exclusion was associated with more than a threefold increase in the odds of reporting an NSSI urge, after adjusting for borderline severity. While the data more clearly supported a baseline negative appraisal bias associated with borderline severity (even under objectively favorable feedback) evidence for cross-level moderation effects remained inconclusive. Social media ostracism emerges as a relevant interpersonal stressor for individuals with NSSI, producing detectable shifts in online engagement and, in exploratory analysis, increases in self-harm urges and changes. Borderline severity tracked a sustained negative interpretation of social feedback, although potential moderation effects regarding exclusion reactivity remained inconclusive. These findings establish Socializapp as a feasible paradigm and highlight everyday digital social experiences as meaningful targets for understanding short-term fluctuations in NSSI vulnerability.

title: Single cell RNA sequencing and emerging transcriptomic technologies in Alzheimer's disease cerebral organoids: a mini review.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most common cause of dementia worldwide, presents a formidable challenge due to its complex, multifactorial etiology, and limited translational success of existing models. Recent advances in stem cell biology have enabled the generation of three-dimensional human cerebral organoids which exhibit multicellular complexity and self-organisation, recapitulating key aspects of fetal brain development in vitro. This mini review highlights the landscape of AD modelling in human cerebral organoids. While studies using single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) form the core of this review, we also discuss single-nucleus RNA sequencing, computational deconvolution, and spatial approaches as translationally relevant extensions. We categorise current organoid research into distinct model types: (1) familial AD models driven by APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 mutations; (2) sporadic AD models incorporating genetic APOE variants and environmental risk factors (serum exposure, pollutants, and viral reactivation); (3) tauopathy models highlighting astrocyte-driven metabolic disruption; (4) models featuring glial-immune interactions; and (5) emerging models of mitochondrial dysfunction as an early disease initiator. Across these categories, single cell technologies reveal critical alterations in lipid metabolism, synaptic programs, and glial-immune crosstalk. Finally, we review methodological innovations-drawing on non-AD developmental organoid studies such as region-specific patterning, morphodynamic control, and enhanced cellular diversity, which offer a roadmap for improving the physiological fidelity of next-generation AD organoid models. Ultimately, integrating these advanced cerebral organoid platforms with single cell technologies offer a powerful toolkit to dissect early disease mechanisms and accelerate the development of personalised therapeutics.

title: Misophonia in adolescents: clinical correlates and associations with autism-related behavioral characteristics within a clinical context.
abstract: Misophonia is characterized by intense emotional and behavioral reactions to specific sounds and has been associated with psychiatric symptoms and sensory sensitivity. This study investigated the prevalence of misophonia in a clinical adolescent outpatient sample and examined its associations with psychiatric symptoms and autism-related behavioral characteristics. The study included 200 adolescents aged 12-18 years who were referred to a child and adolescent psychiatry outpatient clinic. Psychiatric diagnoses were assessed using the Kiddie Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia for School-Age Children-Present and Lifetime Version for DSM-5. Misophonia severity was evaluated with the Amsterdam Misophonia Scale-Revised, while emotional-behavioral problems and autism-related behavioral characteristics were assessed using the Youth Self-Report/11-18. Group comparisons were performed using the chi-squared test, Fisher's exact test, and the Mann-Whitney U test. Spearman's correlation analyses and hierarchical logistic regression analyses were conducted. Adolescents with misophonia had higher rates of major depressive disorder. They also had significantly higher internalizing and externalizing symptoms and elevated autism-related behavioral characteristics than those without misophonia (all p < 0.001; Z = -5.62, -4.59, and - 5.70, respectively). Hierarchical logistic regression analysis revealed that higher internalizing problem scores independently predicted the presence of misophonia (Nagelkerke R² = 0.226, p < 0.001; OR = 1.07). Misophonia in adolescents appears to be closely associated with broader internalizing psychopathology and emotional-behavioral difficulties within psychiatric outpatient settings. Elevated autism-related behavioral characteristics in adolescents with misophonia support further research into the relationship between misophonia and neurodevelopmental characteristics. Such research may contribute to improving clinical assessment and understanding of behavioral patterns associated with misophonia. However, study limitations and inconsistencies in the literature highlight the need for further research in this area.

title: Efficacy and safety of non-hormonal pharmacotherapies for depressive and anxiety symptoms during the menopausal transition and postmenopause: a systematic review.
abstract: Non-hormonal pharmacotherapies are widely used to manage depressive and anxiety symptoms in peri- and postmenopausal women, but comparative evidence across drug classes remains heterogeneous. To systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of non-hormonal pharmacological interventions for depressive and anxiety symptoms during the menopausal transition and postmenopause. A systematic review of six databases and trial registries identified randomized and non-randomized studies evaluating SSRIs, SNRIs, gabapentinoids, and other pharmacotherapies. Due to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, a structured Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) approach was applied. A total of Thirty-one studies (n = 8,124 participants) were included. SNRIs showed more frequent positive effects on depressive symptoms compared with other pharmacological classes, while SSRIs demonstrated modest and variable effects. Gabapentinoids consistently improved vasomotor symptoms but showed limited and low-certainty effects on mood outcomes. Evidence for anxiety outcomes was inconsistent across all drug classes. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. Non-hormonal pharmacotherapies may provide benefit for mood symptoms during the menopausal transition and postmenopause, particularly SNRIs; however, conclusions are limited by heterogeneity, indirectness, and lack of head-to-head comparative trials. Not applicable.

title: Integrating task-state electroencephalography and motor function for intelligent assessment of recovery status from prolonged disorders of consciousness.
abstract: Accurately assessing recovery in patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness (PDoC) is essential for evaluating the therapeutic efficacy and optimizing clinical care. However, substantial individual variability and poorly understood recovery mechanisms render this task exceptionally challenging. We collected task-state electroencephalography and clinical records from 78 PDoC patients to develop an intelligent assessment framework. Power spectral densities (PSDs) and coherence values (CVs) derived from event-related potentials (ERPs) were extracted and integrated with motor function scores to construct a multidimensional feature set. Linear support vector machine (SVM) and logistic regression (LR) models were built and rigorously evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was utilized for visual explanation. The LOOCV indicated that both LR and SVM achieved optimal, similar performance in integrating alpha-band features with motor function (Macro-Average F1-score [Ma-F]: 76.79% versus 75.54%). The Receiver Operating Characteristic curves (with Area Under the Curve values of 77.57% for LR and 72.82% for SVM) and Precision-Recall curves (with Average Precision values of 68.87% for LR and 59.85% for SVM) suggested that the framework performs stably. The reliability curves indicated that both models demonstrate good calibration and are reliable for assessment. The study provides preliminary evidence that alpha-band PSDs and CVs derived from ERPs potentially enhance the motor function assessment performance. This integrated paradigm provides a valuable indicator. Overall, our findings suggest that combining neuroscience with intelligent technology holds promise for improving personalized diagnosis and optimizing the PDoC management.

title: Mental health-related presentations to Australian hospital emergency departments by children and young people, before and after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: COVID-19 pandemic-related 'lockdowns' (i.e., measures to restrict movements) used to reduce the spread of the COVID-19 virus may have impacted how children and young people (CYP) utilised mental health services. The aim of this review was to synthesise research on COVID-19-related changes in mental health-related emergency department (ED) presentations by CYP in Australia, with reference to lockdown stringency. We searched five databases for observational studies published after 31/12/2019 examining ED mental health-related presentations by CYP (aged 0-24 years) before and after onset of COVID-19 lockdowns. Studies were stratified by location and the relative restriction stringency, obtained via the Oxford COVID-19 Government Response Tracker. Region level variation was described, with pooled effects calculated using random effects models. Thirteen studies were included; five from New South Wales, four from Victoria (where lockdowns were most stringent), three from Queensland, and one including multiple Australian states. Outcome definitions and exposure periods were heterogeneous. Pooled estimates showed a moderate-to-large increase in monthly rates of eating disorder presentations, slight-to-moderate increases in overall mental health-related presentations and self-harm and suicide-related presentations, and inconclusive evidence for changes in substance-related and addictive disorder and behavioural/neurodevelopmental disorder-related presentations. Heterogeneity of pooled effects was extremely high (I2 = 84.8-99.5%), and the overall certainty of evidence was very low for all outcomes. Findings differed by jurisdiction, but there was insufficient evidence to identify an association between lockdown stringency and ED presentations. CYP ED presentations for eating disorders appear to have increased over the pandemic period, though certainty of evidence was very low. Findings for overall mental health-related presentations and other disorder groups were mixed, with presentations appearing to be lower in Queensland than other states. Future research should prioritise high quality interrupted-time-series analyses of linked and standardised administrative data to better examine the association between specific pandemic policy measures and CYP mental health-related ED utilisation, whilst controlling for potential confounders. This review has been registered with PROSPERO (CRD42022342496).

title: A decade of glyphosate-surfactant poisoning in India: clinical patterns and predictors of mortality.
abstract: Glyphosate-surfactant herbicide (GlySH) poisoning is increasingly reported in low- and middle-income countries, yet data on clinical predictors of mortality remain limited, particularly from the Indian subcontinent. This study aimed to describe the clinical profile of GlySH poisoning and to identify predictors of in-hospital mortality in a tertiary-care setting in South India. We conducted a retrospective observational study of consecutive adult patients with documented oral GlySH ingestion presenting to a tertiary-care emergency department between January 2009 and July 2019. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory variables were extracted from electronic medical records. In-hospital mortality was the primary outcome. Associations between clinical variables and mortality were assessed using Firth's penalised likelihood logistic regression and Fisher's exact test, with odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported. For predictors with complete separation, odds ratios were not estimable, and Fisher's exact p-values are reported. Multivariable analysis was not performed due to the small number of outcome events. A total of 51 patients were included, of whom four (7.8%) died. Most patients were young adults (45.1% aged 25-44 years), male (76.5%), and had suicidal intent (64.7%). Shock (OR 14.67, 95% CI 1.50-143.74), altered sensorium (OR 14.63, 95% CI 1.34-159.23), elevated serum creatinine > 1.4 mg/dL (p = 0.0009), and dialysis requirement (p < 0.001) were associated with in-hospital mortality on univariate analysis. Elevated liver transaminases and respiratory distress were not significantly associated with mortality. In this 10-year cohort, mortality following GlySH poisoning was closely associated with shock, altered sensorium, and early renal dysfunction, reflecting advanced systemic toxicity. These readily identifiable features may assist in risk stratification and triage of high-risk patients in the emergency setting. Given the small number of outcome events, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating, and larger multicentric prospective studies are required to validate these predictors.

title: Early hemodynamic changes after the use of push-dose noradrenaline in patients presenting to the emergency department with septic shock: a descriptive study.
abstract: Although continuous noradrenaline infusion (CNI) is standard vasopressor therapy during the initial resuscitation of patients with septic shock, hemodynamic stabilization may not be immediate. Push-dose noradrenaline (PDNA) has been proposed as a temporary measure while CNI is being established. However, its clinical use, dosing, early hemodynamic response, and short-term safety in the emergency department (ED) are not well described. To address this gap, we conducted a single-center retrospective descriptive study at a tertiary care hospital in Japan in 2019. Adults with Sepsis-3 septic shock who received PDNA in the ED and were admitted to the intensive care unit were included. We assessed the context and dosing of PDNA administration, CNI use, mean arterial pressure (MAP) within 15 min after PDNA administration, and adverse events. Of 91 patients with septic shock, 50 (55%) received PDNA. PDNA was administered at CNI initiation in 25 patients, during CNI dose escalation in 6, and as rescue administration before CNI initiation in 19. The median (interquartile range [IQR]) initial PDNA dose was 20 (20-30) µg. During the 15-minute observation window, 32 (64%) patients received one bolus, 14 (28%) received two, 3 (6%) received three, and 1 (2%) received four. The directly observed median (IQR) MAP was 52 (44-61) mmHg at initial PDNA administration (n = 30) and 62 (50-68) mmHg 1 min later (n = 25). One of 36 patients evaluable for prespecified physiological adverse events experienced an adverse event; however, no serious adverse events were documented. In this single-center retrospective descriptive study, PDNA was most commonly administered at CNI initiation, and administration was followed by an early increase in median MAP. However, the noncomparative design and concurrent resuscitative interventions preclude attribution of this change solely to PDNA administration. No serious adverse events were documented; however, safety assessment was limited owing to missing data and retrospective ascertainment. These findings do not establish the effectiveness or safety of PDNA. Prospective comparative studies with standardized monitoring are required.

title: Mechanosensation of rice root border cells activates serotonin-mediated pre-invasion behaviors in Meloidogyne graminicola via DEG/ENaC channels.
abstract: Plant-parasitic nematodes (PPNs) locate host roots primarily through chemosensation, yet the sensory events that convert root contact into the stylet thrusts required for host penetration remain obscure. Root border cells (RBCs), terminally differentiated cells shed from the root cap, constitute the first point of physical contact between the root and invading nematodes, but whether and how RBCs trigger pre-invasion behaviors is unknown. Here we showed that rice (Oryza sativa) RBCs induce preparasitic second-stage juveniles (pre-J2) of the rice root-knot nematode Meloidogyne graminicola to exhibit stylet thrusting, feeding behaviors, and marked up‑regulation of the serotonin biosynthesis gene Mg‑tph‑1 in a density‑dependent manner. Among RBC components, the insoluble polysaccharide cellulose is the predominant inducer. We identified two Degenerin/Epithelial Sodium Channel (DEG/ENaC) mechanosensory genes, Mg‑del‑1 and Mg‑unc‑105, both highly expressed in infective J2. RNA interference targeting either gene reduced nematode motility and abolished RBC‑ or cellulose‑induced stylet thrusting and feeding. Furthermore, silencing Mg‑del‑1 or Mg‑unc‑105 downregulated the serotonergic pathway genes Mg‑unc‑43 and Mg‑tph‑1, and markedly reduced 5‑HT immunoreactivity in J2 responding to mechanical stimulation. We propose that specific DEG/ENaC channels mediate the mechanosensing of RBCs or root cellulose by root‑knot nematodes, activating a downstream serotonergic circuit that drives stylet thrusting. This work uncovers a previously uncharacterized mechanosensory pathway in plant‑nematode interactions and identifies nematode DEG/ENaC channels as promising targets for disrupting parasitism, offering a new mechanosensory‑based strategy for nematode control.

title: Targeting neuronal FKBP5 attenuates mechanical allodynia by suppressing NF-κB-mediated neuroinflammation in an NTG-induced chronic migraine mouse model.
journal: The journal of headache and pain
abstract: Chronic migraine (CM) is a debilitating neurological disorder characterized by persistent trigeminovascular sensitization and neuroinflammation. While FK506-binding protein 51 (FKBP5) modulates spinal neuroinflammation in chronic pain, its specific role in trigeminovascular nociceptive processing and CM pathogenesis remains largely unknown. We used a nitroglycerin (NTG)-induced CM mouse model. Following RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) of total RNA isolated from trigeminal nucleus caudalis (TNC) tissue lysates, target expression was validated via reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. To establish causality, we used a neuron-specific CRISPR-Cas9 editing system for Fkbp5 knockout within the TNC, alongside pharmacological interventions using the specific FKBP5 antagonist SAFit2 and the nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) inhibitor PDTC. Migraine-like behaviors were evaluated using von Frey filaments, coupled with biochemical analyses of NF-κB cascade activation and trigeminovascular neuroinflammation. RNA-seq, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence consistently confirmed a marked upregulation of Fkbp5 mRNA and FKBP5 protein in the TNC of NTG-treated mice, predominantly localized to neurons. Concurrently, significant microglial and astrocytic activation was observed in the TNC. Both neuron-specific Fkbp5 knockout and pharmacological inhibition with SAFit2 significantly attenuated NTG-induced periorbital and hind paw mechanical allodynia. Furthermore, FKBP5 deficiency blunted the NTG-triggered phosphorylation of p65 and IκBα, effectively suppressing the downstream release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-1β (IL-1β), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), as well as the upregulation of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) and c-Fos. Crucially, targeted blockade of the NF-κB cascade with PDTC recapitulated the protective behavioral and biochemical effects of FKBP5 deficiency. We demonstrate that neuronal FKBP5 is significantly associated with CM pathogenesis. FKBP5 sustains mechanical allodynia by activating the NF-κB-mediated neuroinflammatory cascade. Consequently, targeting FKBP5 represents a promising therapeutic strategy for CM.

title: Suicide among children and adolescents in India as a public mental health priority.
abstract: Suicide among children and adolescents (≤ 18 years old) is a growing public health concern in India, contributing to an alarming 6% of total suicides reported in 2022. Despite policy efforts, systemic gaps in prevention, reporting, and mental health infrastructure persist. This paper uses secondary data from the Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India (ADSI) reports (2014-2023) published by the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) to map the key trends and key drivers of suicide among youth in India. Descriptive report estimates on suicide data among individuals aged 0-18 years were categorised by gender, cause, and year. To interpret the underlying drivers of suicide, we applied the Socio-Ecological Model (SEM), which organises risk factors across four levels: individual, interpersonal, community, and societal. Between 2014 and 2023, a total of 100,787 children died by suicide in India, with female children consistently outnumbering males. The most frequently reported causes were family-related problems (25,049), followed by academic failure (12,988), love affairs (12,988), and mental illness (6143). Nearly 29% of suicides were attributed to unknown or "other" causes, indicating gaps in documentation. Suicide among Indian children and adolescents is driven by multifaceted structural and psychosocial factors. A Bronfenbrenner's socio-ecological approach reveals multiple points of intervention, including school-based mental health services, family support programs, anti-stigma initiatives, and community-level capacity building. A coordinated public health response tailored to each SEM level is essential to reverse current trends and safeguard child mental health.

title: Theta-Band Temporal Interference Stimulation Modulates Food Reward Prediction Error Encoding in Individuals with Elevated Food Addiction Symptoms.
abstract: Prediction error (PE) signals support feedback evaluation and adaptive updating, and are closely linked to medial frontal theta dynamics, particularly within dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC)-centered networks. However, evidence linking these oscillatory mechanisms to the modulation of PE encoding remains limited. Here, we tested whether theta-band modulation of a dACC-centered medial frontal network altered trial-level PE encoding during food-reward processing. In a single-blind, sham-controlled pre-post design, individuals with elevated food addiction symptoms performed a food incentive-delay task while undergoing electroencephalographic recordings combined with theta-band temporal interference stimulation. Single-trial analyses revealed that feedback-related negativity (FRN) amplitudes varied as a function of both behavioral and model-derived prediction errors. Critically, theta-band modulation altered FRN-PE coupling, with the effect most pronounced for unfavorable outcomes, whereas anticipatory activity remained unchanged. These findings support the hypothesis that theta-band modulation can alter feedback-related PE encoding within this population and task context.

title: H3K9me3 inhibition reverses Alzheimer's progression by restoring synaptic and immune proteostasis across the brain-retina axis.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Epigenetic dysregulation is increasingly linked to aging and neurodegeneration, yet its contribution to retinal and brain pathology in Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains unclear. We quantified the repressive epigenetic mark histone H3 lysine 9 trimethylation (H3K9me3) in post mortem retinas and brains from donors spanning normal cognition, mild cognitive impairment, and AD dementia. Using a multi-enzyme methyltransferase panel, we characterized the in vitro inhibitory activity of ETP69, an epidithiodiketopiperazine, against suppressor of variegation 3-9 homologue 1 (SUV39H1) and other methyltransferases. In two transgenic AD mouse models (APPswe/PS1dE9 and APPswe/tauP301L/PS1tm1Mpm), we assessed ETP69 effects on cerebral H3 methylation, behavior, AD-like pathology, synaptic integrity, and proteomic profiles. H3K9me3 increased early across the AD continuum in both brain and retina, correlating with cognitive impairment and neuropathological burden. H3K9me3 levels were strongly correlated between matched brains and retinas (r = 0.72, p = 0.0002). ETP69 substantially inhibited SUV39H1 and several other methyltransferases in cell-free assays, while consistently reducing cerebral H3K9me3 in vivo relative to other histone marks assessed. In mice, pharmacological H3K9me3 reduction mitigated AD-like pathology, preserved synapses, and improved short- and long-term cognitive and visual performance. Proteomics revealed that H3K9me3 derepression re-established retinal and brain proteostasis and remodeled innate immune pathways and brain-derived neurotrophic factor/nerve growth factor-inducible protein (BDNF/VGF)-granin signaling. This study identifies H3K9me3 accumulation as a shared, reversible epigenetic contributor to AD across the retina-brain axis; its reduction represents a promising disease-modifying strategy, and the retina may provide an accessible readout of brain epigenetic dysfunction.

title: Sex Education in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Qualitative Analysis of ChatGPT-3.5 Responses to Adolescents' Questions on Romantic Relationships and Sexuality.
abstract: Large language model chatbots, such as ChatGPT, have garnered increasing attention in the field of education, due to its versatility, processing speed, and widespread accessibility. However, its application to sexual education remains understudied, highlighting the need for more research into its potential to support informed decision-making among youth. The current study aimed to document ChatGPT-3.5 responses to adolescents' questions about romantic relationships and sexuality, using a more-than-human netnography approach. To obtain these responses, 393 anonymized emails written in French and English from adolescents aged 14 to 16 were collected from a recognized youth support organization. Data were obtained through ChatGPT-3.5 from January 14 to 31, 2024. The analyses focused on identifying content violations and describing the response formats, followed by a conventional content analysis of ChatGPT-3.5 recommendations. Overall, 17.8% of the emails were flagged as potentially violating ChatGPT-3.5's content policy. Responses were provided in two formats: (1) structured text or (2) continuous text that both included an introduction clarifying the question, normalizing the experience, and/or validating emotions; a list of recommendations; and a conclusion promoting support seeking, and/or a positive outlook. The recommendations aimed to encourage adolescents to embrace authenticity and personal agency, practice self-care and build self-confidence, engage in open communication, develop meaningful relationships, and seek support when needed. The findings highlight ChatGPT's potential to contribute to comprehensive sex education for adolescents seeking information.

title: Effect of glycine-enriched freezing medium on post-thaw quality and fertility of Murrah buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) bull semen.
abstract: This study was designed to evaluate the effect of glycine supplementation (0.0, 5.0, 10.0, 15.0, 20.0 and 25.0 mM) in freezing media on post-thaw quality of buffalo bull spermatozoa. Thirty-six semen ejaculates from six breeding Murrah buffalo bulls were collected using artificial vagina. Ejaculates having ≥ 70% sperm motility, ≤ 20% morphological abnormalities and > 500 million/ml concentration were diluted in Tris-egg yolk extender containing selected concentrations of glycine and control and cryopreserved following established protocol. The post-thaw semen was examined for CASA-based sperm motility and kinematics, viability, plasma membrane integrity, acrosome integrity, mitochondrial membrane potential and LPO.
